stories.title: Brother-in-law kills sister-in-law in Etawah:Eloped and married; man later informs police about body at home
stories.summary: A 35-year-old brother-in-law killed his 18-year-old sister-in-law in Etawah. 4 days ago, on Holi, he had eloped with his sister-in-law to Delhi. There, they got married in a temple. On Saturday morning, he reached home from Delhi. At night, he argued with his sister-in-law, Sunaina. In anger, he killed her by hitting her with bricks. After the incident, he went to the police station with the blood-stained brick. He told the police officers, "I have committed murder. The body is lying at home. Pick it up." The accused Vijay Kushwaha works as a contract mechanic in the Delhi Jal Board. 5 years ago, he had a love marriage with Nisha Kathariya. At that time, too, they had eloped to get married. Both families had later accepted their relationship. Vijay and Nisha also have a 3-year-old son. 2 months ago, Vijay had a dispute with Nisha. Since then, Nisha had been living at her parents' home. Meanwhile, Vijay got into an affair with Nisha's cousin, Sunaina. The entire incident took place in the Karanpura area of Etawah Kotwali. When police reached the house, blood was scattered in the room After accused Vijay surrendered, the police reached his house. The body was lying on the floor in the room. There was blood scattered everywhere. Police informed Sunaina's family. The body was sent for a post-mortem. Accused Vijay Kushwah's parents live with him in Delhi. Due to having a house and land in the village, he used to come here often. Deceased Sunaina's father, Raghuraj, said, 'Vijay used to visit our house daily'. On March 4, Vijay lured and eloped with our daughter. He took her to Delhi and got married there. We spoke to her on the phone and asked her to come home. On Saturday evening, daughter Sunaina called her mother. She said, 'Mom, we will come home, please don't beat us'. Around 3 AM, we got a call from the police station to come to the district hospital. When we reached there, we saw our daughter lying on a stretcher in the hospital. Vijay had killed her. Vijay is much older than my daughter. Police told us that injury marks were found on her body and rope marks on her neck. Sunaina's brother Shivam said - We had told mom many times not to let Vijay come to the house. But no one listened to us. He came one day before Holi. On the day of Holi, he ran away with my sister. They got married in a temple in Delhi and also sent photos and videos. Met sister-in-law while going to convince wife Shivam said - Vijay's character is not good. 5 years ago, he had also eloped and married our aunt's daughter, Nisha. There has been discord between Vijay and Nisha for the last two months. Vijay often used to come to his in-laws' house in Barra village of Baidpura to convince his wife, Nisha. That's where he met Sunaina. Sunaina's house was also in the same village. Gradually, an affair started between the two. After this, Vijay started meeting Sunaina. Kidnapping case was registered Shivam said - When Vijay took Sunaina on March 4, we filed a kidnapping case against him at the Saifai police station. Station House Officer Inspector Yashwant Singh said that the accused himself informed the police about the murder. After this, he was taken into custody. The matter is being investigated. No written complaint has been received from the family yet. Action will be taken as soon as it is received.

stories.title: Sister warned him not to lose career for love:In Moradabad man stabbed sister 84 times for girl who was only an online love
stories.summary: In Moradabad, the engineer brother who stabbed his engineer sister 84 times and killed her, Hardik, has now been sent to jail. During police questioning, he kept making confused statements. He said his Muslim girlfriend was tortured by her family and that her life was ruined because of him. What is shocking is that Hardik (25), who brutally killed his twin sister Himshikha (25) and carried out a deadly attack on his mother for the girl, had never even met her. It was only an online relationship. He used to talk to his girlfriend only on Instagram. CO Civil Lines Kuldeep Kumar Gupta said - During interrogation, Hardik revealed that he had been in a relationship with a Muslim girl from Pune for about one and a half years. They were in touch only through Instagram. They would talk for hours. They had even taken vows to live and die together on Instagram. The police investigation so far has revealed that Hardik wanted to marry his online girlfriend. However, his sister and mother advised him not to be crazy in love, saying this is the age to build a career. Meanwhile, the girlfriend's family also started troubling her. They often started beating her. Police are investigating about the girlfriend. 'Mother was worried alone, so I thought I would kill her' SP City Ranvijay Singh said - After Hardik's arrest, several rounds of interrogation were conducted to understand the motive for murder. However, his behavior appeared psychotic. When asked why he killed his sister, he said, ‘She wanted to control my personal life’. She repeatedly advised me to leave the girl and focus on my career. I tried explaining to her many times to leave me alone, but she wouldn't listen. Sister kept saying what have you become because of one girl. You've even left your job and are always caught up with her. Fed up with my sister's advice and taunts, I killed her. When he was asked why he tried to kill his mother? Hardik said that I thought that after killing my sister, I would go to jail. Mother would be left alone. She would be troubled in that case. So I thought I should kill my mother too. Murdered with vegetable cutting knife Hardik killed his sister with a vegetable cutting knife. After interrogation, the police recovered the knife. Later, he was produced in court, from where he was sent to jail. Meanwhile, the sister's postmortem report came out. A total of 84 wounds were found on Himshikha's body. Heart, liver, kidneys, and ribs were all perforated. There were also 4 knife wounds on the neck. Even her limbs, shoulders, and face had knife wounds. Hardik killed his own twin sister Himshikha with such cruelty and brutality that even the postmortem team was shocked. After the postmortem, Himshikha's dead body was cremated by her maternal uncle Deepu. Police had called relatives by sending information to Badaun. Due to the mother being hospitalized, she could not even see her daughter for the last time. Mother sobbing in hospital, daughter murdered, son sent to jail Mother Neelima is hospitalized after being injured by her son. Hardik had stabbed his mother 6 times with a knife, but Neelima was fortunate to survive. Now her condition is out of danger. In one stroke, Neelima's entire world has been destroyed. Her daughter is dead. Her son is in jail. Thinking about all this, Neelima keeps breaking down in tears on the hospital bed. After killing sister, he told mother, ‘Want to give you a surprise, come home’ According to police, Neelima works as an Assistant Manager at an insurance company office on Delhi Road in Moradabad. On Friday, after killing his sister at home, Hardik went to the office to call his mother. He said, ‘Mom, come home, I want to give you a surprise’. He brought his mother home by car. As soon as the mother opened the gate of the house, blood was spread throughout the house. The blood-soaked, dead body of daughter Himshikha was lying on the bed in the room. She screamed at this. Before Neelima could recover, Hardik launched multiple knife attacks on her as well. Both siblings lived in Gurgaon, brother had quit his job Himshikha and Hardik were twins. After completing engineering, both worked at an IT company in Gurgaon. Himshikha was pursuing an MBA alongside her job. While Hardik also worked at a company for one and a half years. After falling in love with a Gurgaon girl on Instagram, he quit his job and started uploading content on YouTube. Neelima had settled in Moradabad after coming from Badaun According to police, Neelima originally belonged to Jogipur in Badaun. About 30 years ago, she and her husband settled in Moradabad. Around 10 years ago, she separated from her husband. After that, she started living in a rented house in Buddhi Vihar. She educated her children and made them capable of getting jobs.

stories.title: Varanasi woman turns cow dung into livelihood for thousands:Rita Tiwari trains nearly 6,000 women; helps them earn and live with dignity
stories.summary: When intentions are as strong as steel, and the goal is social welfare, even seemingly ordinary resources become a means of extraordinary change. 50-year-old Rita Tiwari, a resident of Tarna Yamuna Nagar Colony in Shivpur police station area of Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh, has proven this to be true. Today, on the auspicious occasion of International Women's Day, Rita Tiwari's story serves as a beacon for millions of women who dream of creating their own identity and becoming self-reliant. Rita Tiwari has transformed cow dung from mere 'waste' into the foundation of an 'economy'. Today, under her guidance, thousands of women in Varanasi are not only supporting their households but also living with dignity in society by making incense sticks, lamps, statues, and planters from cow dung. The idea of 'empowerment' emerged during crisis Rita Tiwari shares that she has been involved in cow service and social work for the past two decades. However, the major change in her life and working style came during the lockdown imposed during the COVID-19 pandemic. Rita explains that when she would go to poor and Dalit settlements to distribute food, she witnessed the helplessness of women there very closely. Due to financial constraints, these women were struggling even for their children's basic needs. This is where Rita had the idea that these women need not just donations, but work. She contacted the Cow Science and Research Center, Nagpur, and learned the intricacies of making valuable products from cow dung. After training, she ordered molds for making incense sticks, statues, and planters, and began her mission. The beginning was small, but the goal was big. Gradually, women kept joining, and today it has become a caravan. Currently, around 6 thousand women from all eight blocks of Varanasi, like Harhua, Cholapur, Chiraigaon, Badagaon, Pindra, Sevapuri, Araji Line, and Kashi Vidyapeeth have joined this institution.

stories.title: Two women perform last rites for the abandoned in UP:Gorakhpur's 'Pushpalata' Muzaffarnagar's 'Shalu' fulfills duty of a son
stories.summary: Every person desires that when they leave this world, they should be carried by their loved ones. The last rites should be performed with full respect and proper rituals. But not everyone is destined for this. Many people pass away in anonymity, with no one to claim their bodies. Two UP women have taken up the responsibility of giving final farewell to such unclaimed bodies. These women are- Pushpalata Singh from Gorakhpur and Shalu Saini from Muzaffarnagar. On International Women's Day, read the story of these two women of how they chose to step away from social traditions and take up this responsibility, and what inspired them to dedicate themselves to this service. An Ailing Elderly Man Changed Her Life Pushpalata who is a resident of Gorakhpur said that about three years ago she saw an elderly man in a very sick condition by the roadside. She did not leave him in that state. Instead, she brought him home with her and arranged treatment for him. She continued his treatment for nearly a year. Later, the elderly man passed away. She herself performed his last rites and this was the moment when the thought came to her mind that those who have no one in this world also deserve a dignified farewell. From then on, she resolved to perform the last rites of unclaimed bodies. Support for poor and helpless people Pushpalata does not limit herself only to performing the last rites of unclaimed bodies. If she finds any helpless or sick person on the road, she takes care of them and, if necessary, even brings them home with her. 5 thousand people joined, 40 people active She said, “Around 5 thousand people have joined my campaign so far. However, only about 35 to 40 people actively work among them”. Police hands over bodies after legal process According to Pushpalata, bodies that have no claimants are handed over to her by the police after the legal formalities are completed. She then prepares for the last rites with full respect. First, she cleans the body and prepares it properly, and then takes it to the cremation ground located on the banks of the Rapti River. There, she personally carries the body to the funeral pyre and completes the entire ritual by lighting the pyre herself. If someone later gets information about their family member and their last rites have been performed by them, they can also receive the ashes. Pledge to donate own body and organs With this same spirit of humanity, Pushpalata has taken another big decision in her life. She has pledged to donate her body and organs while alive. She said that when she is no longer in this world, what could be more satisfying than having her body or organs be useful for someone in need. Her father is no longer in this world, but even when he was alive, he never opposed this decision. Currently, Pushpalata lives alone in her father's house. More than 250 bodies cremated so far Pushaplata says that in 2025, she performed the last rites of 225 bodies. From the beginning of 2026 until now, she has performed the last rites of more than 50 unclaimed bodies. Now read the story of Shalu Saini from Muzaffarnagar, who has performed the last rites of more than 6,000 bodies from the Covid period until now. Where did the inspiration to perform last rites of dead bodies come from Shalu Saini who is a resident of Muzaffarnagar shares that her social service journey began with a sudden incident. She said, “Dead bodies would often flow into the Ganges river in the Shukratal area. This area is considered a Khadar region, which is why bodies flowing in the river were often found here”. One such day when she saw a body that had flowed into the Ganges, a question arose in her mind about who would perform the last rites of these people. From that moment, she decided to give such bodies a respectful final farewell. Many bodies washed away in Kedarnath floods She said that when disaster struck Kedarnath in 2013, people were washed away to different places. During that time, some bodies arrived in their area. People from her organization informed her about it, then she arranged for their last rites. Performing last rites continuously since Covid period She added, “When the Covid pandemic period came, I started this service work continuously”. She said, “During Covid, the most painful time was when many families were afraid to come near or touch the bodies of their own people. The families who worked hard their whole lives for their loved ones, distanced themselves after death”. She further stated, “At that time, there were very few unclaimed bodies, but now they also receive people who don't have money for last rites or who live in slums”. According to Shalu, from the time of Covid until now, she has performed the last rites of more than 6,000 bodies. Collects expenses with help from friends Regarding the expenses incurred in funeral services, she explained, “I collect money with help of my friends and companions. The work continues with whatever support I receive”. Runs home and service through street vending To support her family, she operates a cart selling clothes and fast food at Jhansi ki Rani Chowk. From this income, she manages both her children's expenses and her social service work. Also started an old age home She said that she had a plot in South Krishna Puri area, where she started an old age home named 'Krantikari Shalu Saini'. Arrangements are being made here to house helpless elderly people. Takes ashes to Haridwar every month She stated that she takes the ashes of the bodies whose last rites she performs to Haridwar every month and immerses them in the Ganges. Peace prayers are also conducted there. Sons Also Help She said that her children are the biggest support in her life. They give her full support and never stop her from doing this work. When she is out of town, her 23-year-old son Sumit Saini also fulfills this responsibility and performs the last rites when needed.

stories.title: LKG student kidnapped in front of grandfather in Prayagraj:2 criminals flee after dragging child into car
stories.summary: On Saturday, an LKG student was kidnapped in broad daylight in Prayagraj. The student was returning home from school. As soon as he got out of the school van, two criminals pulled him into a car and fled. This kidnapping happened in front of the child's grandfather. He had come to receive him. He was standing just a short distance away. The family's financial condition is not good. The child's father works as a security guard in Mumbai. The mother is in a terrible state, crying continuously. No ransom call has been received yet. Additional Police Commissioner Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma and Yamunapar DCP Vivek Chandra Yadav reached the spot. Both officers reprimanded Manda police station SHO Anil Kumar Verma. Ajay Pal has assured the recovery of the student within 24 hours. Police teams are engaged in searching for the kidnappers. Now read the complete incident in sequence... School is 15 km away from home The incident occurred around 4 PM on Saturday evening in Sarai Kala village of Manda. Om Prakash Sharma from the village works as a security guard in Mumbai. His wife, two children, and his father, Nageshwar, live in the village. Among Om Prakash's two children, Prateek is the elder one, 6 years old. He has a younger sister who is 3-years-old. Prateek studies in LKG at Sonar Ka Tara School located in Ramnagar, Meja. The school is about 15 km away from home, and he travels by van. The van drops him about 150 meters away from his house, from where his grandfather picks him up and drops him off. Criminals came in white Alto car Grandfather Nageshwar said - Prateek returns home from school around 4 PM every evening. On Saturday evening, too, I was going to pick him up at the same time. I was about 20 steps away from the point where the school van drops off Prateek. Just then, a white Alto car came and stopped. Two people were sitting in it. One came out of the car and started asking me for directions. At that moment, the van arrived. He explained that as soon as Prateek got out of the van, the person who was asking me for directions quickly ran towards the child. Before I could understand anything, his accomplice moved the car forward, and in the next moment, they pulled Prateek into the car and fled with their companion. I ran after them but couldn't reach the car. Grandfather said - Couldn't see the car number Police arrived after being informed about this incident that occurred in broad daylight. During questioning, the grandfather said that everything happened so quickly that he couldn't see the car number. He had never seen either of the criminals before. When police questioned the villagers, they learned that the car went towards Aunta village. Police set up checkpoints on all nearby roads, but so far no trace of the kidnappers, and the child has not been found. DCP Yamunanagar Vivek Chandra Yadav said, So far in the questioning, the family has not mentioned any enmity. The family's financial condition is not very good. Till now, no calls have been received by the family members. Investigation is being conducted on every point. Akhilesh Yadav demands safe return of the child home

stories.title: YouTuber Anurag Dobhal crashes car during Instagram Live:‘UK07 Rider’ survives high-speed ‘final drive’ in apparent 'suicide' bid
stories.summary: Famous YouTuber from Dehradun Anurag Dobhal allegedly attempted suicide during an Instagram live on Saturday evening. Around 7 PM, he went live while driving his car on the Meerut highway in Uttar Pradesh. During the live session, he appeared emotional and said, “Let’s go for the final drive.” He was also seen slapping himself repeatedly while speaking about his mother. At one point he said, “Next time I come, just give me love.” Soon after, Anurag reportedly accelerated the car to nearly 150 kmph and crashed it into a divider. The Instagram live ended immediately after the collision. Anurag Dobhal is widely known online as UK07 Rider and had also participated in Bigg Boss 17. He sustained injuries in the crash and has been admitted to Shubharti Hospital in Meerut, where he is currently undergoing treatment. See PHOTOS related to the incident... “Mom, give me love when I come next time” In the Instagram live video, Anurag emotionally said, “Mom, when I come in the next life, just give me love… I really needed love. There are no people left now, who should I call?” After saying this, he added, “Let’s go for the final drive.” In the video, he is seen playing an English song in the car and accelerating rapidly. Within moments, the speed touches around 144 kmph. During the drive, he suddenly turns the steering wheel, seemingly attempting to hit the divider. However, the live video abruptly stops at that moment. Second video surfaces, Anurag seen crying on the road Another video from the scene has also surfaced on social media. In the footage, Anurag’s car appears badly damaged, and he is seen lying on the road while people nearby rush to help him. Wearing a yellow T-shirt, Anurag is seen crying in pain as bystanders pull him out of the car and assist him. Had shared emotional 2-hour video four days ago Just four days before the incident, on March 4, Anurag had uploaded a nearly two-hour-long video on his YouTube channel. In the video, he opened up about his personal life struggles, including family disputes, marriage issues, leaving home, financial problems and mental stress. Throughout the video, he became emotional several times and even broke down while speaking. He said his life had changed drastically in recent years and that circumstances forced him to make his personal story public. Anurag also played audio recordings and conversations with family members in the video, stating that he had been dealing with mental stress for a long time.

stories.title: Ashutosh Maharaj attacked in moving train:Claims attacker tried to cut his nose; blames Shankaracharya’s disciple for assault
stories.summary: Ashutosh Maharaj, who had filed an FIR alleging sexual harassment of batuks against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, was reportedly attacked in a moving train on Sunday. According to Ashutosh Maharaj, he was travelling from Ghaziabad to Prayagraj on the Rewa Express and was seated in the First AC coach. He said that at around 5 am, when the train was near Sirathu railway station, he got up to go to the toilet. A man was standing near the door outside. Assault with sharp weapon Ashutosh Maharaj said that when he moved ahead, the attacker suddenly assaulted him from behind. The assailant allegedly tried to cut his nose with a sharp weapon and repeatedly struck his face and hands. He sustained serious injuries and lost a considerable amount of blood. According to Ashutosh Brahmachari, he somehow managed to escape and locked himself inside the train’s toilet to save his life. From there, he called the Government Railway Police (GRP) and reported the incident. FIR registered, investigation begins Ashutosh Maharaj has held Swami Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand and others responsible for the attack. Acting on the complaint, the GRP has registered an FIR and begun an investigation into the matter. Shankaracharya rejects allegations Responding to the accusations, Shankaracharya said the incident was merely a drama. According to him, Ashutosh was making such claims to create an atmosphere and obtain security protection. He said the allegations against him were intended only to attract media attention and divert focus from the ongoing journey. Ashutosh Maharaj hits back Shortly afterwards, Ashutosh Maharaj responded sharply to the Shankaracharya’s remarks. He said every drop of blood would be avenged through legal means. He claimed the attacker had said that his nose would be cut and offered at the feet of his 'guru'. Ashutosh said they would fight the matter through the law. Rejecting the counter-claims, he said it was absurd to suggest that someone would stage an attack on themselves and added that the Shankaracharya should try getting his own nose cut to understand..

stories.title: Two brothers killed YouTuber Salim Wastik over his controversial videos:3-min struggle leaves YouTuber with 14 wounds; attackers flee, later killed in police encounters
stories.summary: February 27, 2026, Friday. At 7:30 AM, Zeeshan and Gulfam reached the Loni area of Ghaziabad. They attacked ex-Muslim Salim Wastik (YouTuber). One had a paper cutter, the other had a knife. The entire attempt was to behead. The struggle continued for 3.5 minutes. Salim suffered 14 serious wounds on his neck, stomach, back, and chest. During this time, a woman arrived and raised an alarm. At this, both attackers fled. Pictures appeared in the Telegram group, stating that Salim, an Ex-Muslim, has been taken to the hospital. Both kept a fast the next day. Police identified both based on CCTV, vehicle numbers, and presence at the scene. When the search began, a confrontation occurred. Police killed Zeeshan in an encounter on March 1 and Gulfam on March 3. How was this incident planned? Who was behind the planning? Why did Zeeshan want rights to the Babri Masjid? Read Sunday Big Story... Salim left Islam and became an atheist 7 years ago Ghaziabad's Salim Vastik's original home is in Shamli district. 20 years ago, he left Shamli and settled in the Ashok Vihar area of Loni in Ghaziabad. Besides him, his family includes his wife and his son, Usman Khan. Salim previously worked in construction-related work. He also worked as a Maulvi for some time. Later, he became disillusioned with Islam. He left Islam and added 'Vastik' to his name. Salim bought land about one and a half kilometers away from his house in Ali Garden Colony, then built a house there. He opened his office in it and started working there. Salim had agreements with different TV channels, where he used to go for religious debates. He would debate there as an ex-Muslim. He would discuss matters related to Islam. Later, he created his YouTube channel and would comment about Islam on it. Misconduct in Jammu-Kashmir, Channel Deleted On April 22, 2025, a terrorist attack occurred in the Basran Valley of Pahalgam in Anantnag district of Jammu-Kashmir. 26 tourists were killed after being asked about their religion. This incident was condemned worldwide. Salim reached Jammu-Kashmir with his companions Aamir and Ahsan. They protested against this incident there. They spoke with some media personnel. They talked about boycotting Kashmir. Because of this, they became targets of local people. They were beaten up, and their social media accounts were forced to be deleted. Salim complained about this to the Jammu and Kashmir Police, but the police took no action. After this, Salim returned to Ghaziabad. He complained to the police here, but the police did not take action, saying it was a Kashmir matter. After this, Salim created another channel in his own name. Regarding the Pahalgam attack, Salim had said to a news channel - If we speak from our perspective, this was wrong. It is a terrorist attack, it is against humanity. But, if we look from Islam's perspective, they have done a virtuous deed. This is the work of Shabab. After the Kashmir incident, Salim became a target of extremists. On the other hand, Salim also started making more aggressive videos compared to before. At the beginning of the videos, he would often use offensive words. He would talk about Halala, Hadith, and Triple Talaq. While discussing these topics, he would quote verses from the Quran. Many people from the Muslim community would write abusive comments and give threats on these videos. They offered prayers before going to attack Salim Zeeshan (23) and Gulfam (42), who attacked Salim Wastik (50), were residents of Saidnagli town in Amroha. Their father, Buniyad Ali, works with wood. Both of them also did the same work. In Buniyad's family, besides these two sons, there are 5 daughters. Buniyad Ali has gotten all of them married. Gulfam was the eldest, and Zeeshan was the youngest. In 2013, Gulfam left Amroha and settled in the Khoda area of Ghaziabad. Here he lived in a rented room at the house of a person named Ali Hasan in Mangal Bazaar. After 2021, Zeeshan also went to Ghaziabad to join Gulfam. He worked in a company. Zeeshan studied at a local madrasa in Amroha. Then he passed 12th from a nearby inter-college. He grew a beard. He started actively participating in Islamic programs. He would make videos on social media, talking about Islam. In one video, he had talked about claiming rights to the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya. When Gulfam and Zeeshan would watch Salim's videos, they would become red with anger. Both brothers were also connected to some WhatsApp and Telegram groups. They would comment there. The other people there would talk about beheading. According to police sources, these two brothers had planned to kill Salim just 15 days ago. For this, they had chosen the holy month of Ramadan and Friday. On the morning of February 27, both were in their rented room. They had offered Fajr prayer (morning prayer) at 5:30 in the morning. Focus was on killing Salim by slitting his throat After this, Zeeshan and Gulfam took out their cousin's KTM bike. They reached Ali Garden Colony about 20 kilometers away. Both of them knew about both Salim's house and office. They knew when he came and went, at what time. At 7:54 in the morning, both reached Salim's office. At that time, Salim was lying on the sofa watching videos on his mobile. Both brothers went inside. Zeeshan first took out a paper cutter, and then Gulfam also took out a knife. Both brothers were focused entirely on Salim's throat. They both wanted to cut Salim's throat with full force. Salim was continuously screaming. During this, Gulfam says to Zeeshan, 'Kill him, don't be afraid.' After this, Zeeshan picked up a glass table lying there and broke it. Then he launched repeated attacks on Salim with his sharp pieces. The glass from the table got embedded in Salim's back. The CCTV footage that has emerged is 3 minutes and 39 seconds long. Zeeshan and Gulfam were still inside at that time. Sent attack photos to group, then went home After the attack, both took photos and videos of Salim suffering. They sent it to their people. The same picture also appeared on a Telegram channel called Muslim Army. This group has more than 18,300 members. It contained two photos. One was a smiling photo of Salim, with text below saying - Ex-Muslim Salim, treatment video coming soon... After the attack, another picture came where Salim was badly injured. Its caption read - Salim, an ex-Muslim, has been taken to the hospital. Want the full video? Many people in this comment group reacted to this. Zeeshan and Gulfam left Salim's office after carrying out the incident. In this attack, Zeeshan's finger was also slightly cut. This caused blood to get on the clothes. Both went back towards their room. However, on the way, a person recorded a video of these two, considering them suspicious. This video came to light later. After reaching the room, both brothers changed their clothes. Then they reached their home in Saidnagali in Amroha by bike. Here, the elder brother, Gulfam, stayed for some time. Then he went back to Ghaziabad by bike. While, Zeeshan stayed in the village. He fasted the whole day and had iftar with the family in the evening. He took leave every Friday, so the family did not suspect Zeeshan was religiously orthodox. That's why he took leave on Friday instead of Sunday. He came home every week. Therefore, family members did not suspect that he had come after attacking someone. The next day, Zeeshan kept another fast. After the morning prayer, he caught a bus to Ghaziabad. In the afternoon, he talked to his mother on the phone and spoke about offering prayers. On the other hand, after this high-profile incident, 10 police teams were formed. 70 personnel were engaged in searching for Salim's attackers. Crime Branch and STF also became active. A total of 210 CCTVs were examined. The mobile network was investigated at the scene. By February 28, police had discovered that this incident was carried out by Zeeshan and Gulfam. On the night of March 1, both were seen coming in the Loni area itself. When Station In-charge Nitin Chaudhary tried to stop them, firing broke out. About 25 to 30 rounds were fired in 15 minutes. Zeeshan was hit by one bullet in the chest and one in the leg. However, Gulfam escaped. Police took Zeeshan to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. On March 3, police surrounded Gulfam in the Indirapuram police station area. He also opened fire. However, he was killed in retaliatory police firing. This means both brothers were killed in police encounters within 48 hours. Gulfam was hot-tempered, Zeeshan was calm but cunning Upon talking to people living near their homes in Amroha, it was revealed that Gulfam had an angry temperament. Whereas Zeeshan remained calm. He actively participated in Islamic religious events. He would collect donations in the neighborhood. He made Islamic videos on social media. There are also discussions that both of them used to attend the Jamaat. They would meet Muslims coming from different countries across the world. The way Salim was attacked, 2 similar murders have taken place in the last few years. First- Umesh Kolhe was murdered in Amravati, Maharashtra. On June 21, 2022, 54-year-old Umesh had posted in a WhatsApp group supporting BJP spokesperson Nupur Sharma's comments on Prophet Muhammad. This became the main reason. Yusuf, associated with Tabligi Jamaat, killed Umesh Kolhe by slitting his throat in the middle of the road. Umesh had known Yusuf for 16 years. Umesh had also helped in Yusuf's wedding. Police had arrested 10 more people in this case. Second- Just 7 days after the murder of Umesh Kolhe, Kanhaiya Lal Teli was murdered in the Udaipur district of Rajasthan. Gaus Mohammad and Mohammad Riyaz came on a bike and started making a video. After this, both of them slit Kanhaiya's throat and killed him. Kanhaiya had posted a comment by Nupur Sharma on his Facebook. This became the reason for his murder, too. Both main accused are in jail. NIA is handling this case. Court had objected to 'Sar Tan Se Juda' This slogan of 'Sar Tan Se Juda' has been going on in the country for a long time. However, after the Nupur Sharma case came up in 2022, it started being chanted continuously. There was violence in Bareilly, and slogans were raised. This slogan was also raised there. The situation became such that the Allahabad High Court had to object to this slogan. The single bench of Judge Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal had rejected the bail application of Rehan, who was arrested during the violent protest in Bareilly. The judge said - Such violent slogans raised in the name of Islam are completely contrary to Prophet Muhammad's ideals. If a follower of Islam raises slogans about beheading someone for insulting the Prophet, it is an insult to the Prophet Muhammad's ideals. This slogan is not connected to India's cultural, legal, and religious traditions. It is influenced by blasphemy laws and violent incidents in the neighboring country. The judge had said - Religious slogans like Jai Shri Ram and Nara-e-Takbir are not a crime if they are not being used to intimidate someone or incite violence. However, if they are being used to incite violence, then it is wrong. Maulana said - What happened was wrong, religious comments should not have been made Darul Uloom's Firangi Mahal spokesperson, Maulana Sufyan Nizami, says - Whatever happened was wrong. However, the law does not give anyone the right to speak inappropriately about anyone's religion. What Salim was saying fills people with anger. Educated people respond like educated people, but those who are uneducated, or let's say those who are instigated, become violent. Sufyan says that we need to ensure that the administration takes timely action against those who speak inappropriately about any religion. However, even after the encounter of Zeeshan and Gulfam, the police investigation has not ended yet. Efforts are being made to get to the bottom of this case. Their Pakistan connections are being investigated. Attempts are being made to contact people present in that Telegram group.

stories.title: Brick kiln worker’s son becomes IAS:Vimal Kumar from Raebareli secures 107th rank in UPSC; celebrates with 7-km procession
stories.summary: Ramdev’s son Vimal Kumar, who worked at a brick kiln in Raebareli, has become an IAS officer, securing 107th rank in UPSC. To celebrate his success, Vimal led a 7-kilometre procession with a convoy. His convoy included 12 cars, a DJ system and more than 50 bikes. People welcomed Vimal at several places and garlanded him with flowers. Father Ramdev’s eyes welled up with tears at his son’s achievement. Speaking about his success, Vimal Kumar said, “A DM madam once visited Navodaya Vidyalaya. That’s when I decided to become an IAS officer.” To keep expenses low, he took online classes three times while staying in the village. Read Vimal Kumar’s journey to becoming an IAS officer. First see 3 pictures... Ramdev lives in Chandemau village of Khiro block in Raebareli district. He has 3 sons and 2 daughters. Vimal Kumar (30) is the youngest son. On his son becoming an IAS, Ramdev says - Very happy. I educated my son by working as a laborer at brick kilns and doing sharecropping. Dainik Bhaskar team reached Chandemau village, 32 kilometers away from district headquarters. At that time, Vimal Kumar was seated in a car. Family members and villagers were showering flowers on him. DJ was playing in the background. As Vimal's convoy moved forward, more cars and bikes joined the procession. Gradually, more than 12 cars and over 50 bikes joined the convoy. People kept stopping Vimal to shower flowers and garland him. The 7-kilometer procession lasted for about 2 hours. After this, the village locals brought Vimal Kumar home. The number of well-wishers at home was continuously increasing. We spoke with Vimal's elder brother Ajit Kumar. Ajit says - the family's financial condition is very modest. I myself work as a laborer in Raebareli. Despite financial constraints, we never let any obstacles come in the way of Vimal's education. We continuously encouraged him. Vimal's sister-in-law says - this success has come after many struggles. There were many difficulties and obstacles at home, but Vimal did not give up his goal. He had come during Holi. When the result came yesterday, he said "Bhabhi, my result is out. I have been selected." Buffaloes tied at the door, house was recently plastered Vimal's house is half permanent and half temporary. There are 5 rooms, out of which only 2 are permanent. Vimal's elder brother has gone abroad to earn, which has improved the financial condition of the house. After this, the front part of the house has been plastered. Two buffaloes are tied outside their house. Besides this, there is a fodder cutting machine and hay stored. From village primary school to IIT Family members say, “Vimal Kumar completed his early education from the village primary school Chandemau. After this, he was selected in Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Maharajganj. He studied there till 10th class. For further studies, he went to Kerala and then reached Delhi for higher education.” In 2020, Vimal Kumar obtained his B.Tech degree from IIT Delhi. After this, he started preparing for UPSC examination. He did not take help from any big coaching institute for this. He mostly prepared through self-study while staying in Raebareli. Vimal explains - Appeared for UPSC exam continuously from 2021 to 2025. Continued preparation without coaching even during the Corona pandemic. In the first 4 attempts, reached the interview stage but couldn't get final selection. Even after this, I didn't give up. Prepared while staying in Lucknow and cleared the interview in the 5th attempt. This time I got 107th rank. Did online preparation, faced failure for 4 years Vimal Kumar says - Online preparation reduced expenses. I faced failure continuously for 4 years. Last year (in 2024) I gave the interview, where I missed selection by 12 marks. Felt very discouraged after failing. Despite this, I didn't give up. Tried once again and passed. Vimal Kumar says - Regular study, discipline and proper use of time is the real key to success. stories.title: Stray dogs maul 8-year-old girl to death in Lucknow:Body found 500 meters away from house in a field, flesh hanging
stories.summary: Stray dogs killed an 8-year-old girl by mauling her in Lucknow. The blood-soaked body of the girl was found in a field about 500 meters away from home. Her face was completely mutilated. Pieces of flesh were hanging from various places. The incident occurred around 6 PM on Sunday in Tarauna village of the Rahimabad police station area. The deceased was identified as Anshika. She was a class 1 student. She had left home alone when the dogs attacked her. Some women from Tarauna village had gone towards the fields in the evening. During this time, they saw someone lying on the ground in the field. The women got scared and came to the village to tell people about this. Upon receiving the information, villagers reached the field with sticks. The villagers saw that Anshika's blood-soaked body was lying in the field. Dogs were sitting in a pack at some distance The villagers said that after this, we informed Anshika's family members about this. The family members reached the spot and brought the body home with our help. They also informed the police. The villagers said that where Anshika's body was lying, fierce dogs were sitting at some distance from there. Those dogs were from the neighboring village. Face badly mauled, flesh torn apart Villagers said that no one saw when the dogs were mauling the girl. But looking at the girl's body, it's clear that she was attacked by dogs. There were marks of dog bites on the girl's face. Her face was completely mauled. Pieces of flesh were torn out in several places. There were dog paw prints at the spot where the body was found. Anshika was the youngest among 3 siblings Anshika was the youngest of three children of her parents. Her father, Dilip Kashyap, said that Anshika had left home in the evening. A while later, they received news of her death. Mother Soni fainted upon seeing the body. Other family members are also in terrible condition, crying continuously.

Saharanpur man kills friend to fake his own death:Body burnt in car as part of plan to dodge rape case
stories.summary: A young man killed his friend to fake his own death in Saharanpur. He placed the body in a car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. The accused did this to escape punishment in a rape case. After the incident, the accused fled to Dehradun. To hide his identity, the main accused got his hair cut. He got a new SIM card and called his brother to file a missing person report, so that police would consider him dead. The brother filed the missing person report. On February 25, a burnt body was found in an Alto car near the Kali River in Amrapur forest by the roadside. When police investigated, the case was uncovered. On February 28, four people, including the main accused, were arrested. During interrogation, the accused confessed to their crime. The case belongs to the Gagalhedi police station area. SSP Abhinandan said that on February 25, the village head of Chaurakhurd informed the police that a burnt Alto car was standing near a culvert on the Chandpur road. In which there was a burnt body of a person. The police and the field unit reached the spot and started an investigation. The car was identified based on its burnt number. Investigation revealed that the car had been sold multiple times. The young man named Arjun had last purchased it on February 16, 2026. Meanwhile, Arjun's brother Vijay Sagar reached the police station and informed that Arjun has been missing since February 24. His phone is switched off. Police started the investigation. Meanwhile, on February 27, Babita, a resident of Mohammadpur Kandhela village, reached the police station with her son Akshay and other family members. She said that my son Rohit has been missing for 5 days. Arjun, whose body was found in the car, was Rohit's friend. He used to visit his house. DNA test revealed the body was Rohit's Babita had told the police that Rohit had borrowed ₹1.60 lakh from Arjun. Which he was unable to repay. Police became suspicious. Police intensified the investigation. Police conducted a DNA test on the dead body found in the car. DNA matched with the family members. The dead body found in the car was Rohit's. Police handed over the body to the family. Now police started searching for Arjun. Police began monitoring Vijay Sagar, the brother who had filed Arjun's missing report. The number was put under surveillance. Meanwhile, it was discovered that Arjun was alive. He was living in Dehradun. On February 28, Arjun came to meet his younger brother Vijay Sagar. Police arrested both of them near the Badkala flyover. Now read the accused's confession... When the police interrogated him, Arjun told the truth. Arjun said - In 2024, I raped a minor in Dehradun. I went to jail in that case. I was afraid that I might get sentenced. So I made a plan to fake my death to escape. In jail, I met Sarik. He was imprisoned in a kidnapping case. Friendship with Rohit began in July 2025 A year later, I got out of jail on bail. Then I started working at a private finance company in Jhabreda. During this time in July, I became friends with Rohit. I got him addicted to alcohol. Then I lent him about ₹1.60 lakh. After this, on the night of February 24, I took Rohit with me. My other companions, Robin and Sarik, were also with me. We made Rohit drink alcohol. When he was intoxicated, we strangled him to death with a muffler. After this, we placed the body on the driver's seat of the Alto car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. So that it would appear that Arjun died in an accident. Police have recovered a Kia Sonet car from the accused.

stories.title: ‘No action for cows, we will launch religious fight’:Shankaracharya adds, 'Yogi not proving himself to be Hindu'
stories.summary: ‘40 days time was given, 30 days have passed, but Yogi has not proved himself as a true Hindu. No effort has been made for ’Gau Mata'. Therefore, we will have to declare a religious war for the dignity of 'Gau Mata'. We will have to draw a line to see who is in favour of the cow and who is against it.' It has become necessary that after 40 days, on the 41st day, we should go to Lucknow and announce the beginning of the religious war for the dignity of ‘Gau Mata’. In the remaining 10 days, there will be a final wait of hope. After that, on March 11, after the period of 40 days is over, it will be necessary to make the announcement.' Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand said this while targeting CM Yogi. He said that from March 11, they will declare a religious war in Lucknow to declare ‘Gau Mata’ as the national mother. Regarding Israel and America's attack on Iran, Shankaracharya said that when hypocrisy increases, such wars happen. If there is a religious war, there will be no need for such physical wars. We responded in 12 hours; they couldn't respond even in 30 days Shankaracharya said - We were asked to explain within 24 hours how we could call ourselves Shankaracharya? We answered in 12 hours. After that, to investigate whether some 'Kalnemi' have entered our society. We had asked Adityanath ji, who is handling the responsibility of the Chief Minister wearing saffron clothes, to explain how you are a real Hindu. Tell us in 40 days. When 10 days passed, we assessed whether these people did anything in these 10 days or not. When 20 days passed, we assessed again. Today, after 30 days have passed, we have again assessed whether they have gained any clarity about being Hindu. Have they done anything about the demand of the country's Sanatani people regarding ‘Gau Mata’? Sadly, 30 days have passed, and so far, no such effort has been seen from their side for ‘Gau Mata’. Yes, during this time, Yogi was abroad for almost a week. Now, he can say that I wasn't even here. However, you cannot make excuses to go abroad by ignoring the sentiments of the majority of people in your country. Therefore, it has been confirmed that no effort was made by them. Read what he said about the America-Israel and Iran issue Shankaracharya said - Wars keep happening all the time. Sometimes with weapons, sometimes for power balance. Every country keeps making plans against the others. But just because there's a war somewhere, should we abandon protecting our dharma? Should we give permission to slaughter and eat cows because war has broken out? Sell them, satisfy the British. Cut up our mother cow and serve it to them. This is why our ancestors participated in the freedom struggle to drive out the British. So that when they leave, we can slaughter cows and send them. This is such a despicable thing. This war is happening because religious wars have stopped. When there is religious war, people will have respect for religion in their minds. The hypocrisy that is happening in the name of religion will end. Such wars happen when hypocrisy increases. The President of America says that we should get the Nobel Peace Prize. He also makes all the arrangements for war. This is hypocrisy. When such hypocrisy spreads in the world. When hypocrisy is not controlled, such wars happen. Therefore, religious war is very necessary, so that such material wars do not happen. People should not suffer loss of life and property. We do not wish for peace; let the heat come out, so that peace happens automatically. Therefore, let it happen. Read the latest case of ongoing controversy regarding Shankaracharya in detail There was a dispute between Shankaracharya and the administration on Mauni Amavasya on January 18 at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. 8 days later, on January 24, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj filed a complaint with the Police Commissioner. In this, allegations of sexual exploitation of children were made during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. A petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8, alleging inaction by the police. On February 13, 2 children were presented in court. Their statements were recorded on February 21. On the court's orders, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station the same day. Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and 2-3 unknown persons were named as accused in the FIR. On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On the 27th, the High Court granted bail to Shankaracharya.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs; UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs The Israeli Air Force said it dropped more than 1,200 bombs on Iran over the past day in joint strikes with the United States, including the attack that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. 2. BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; denied leave for daughter’s wedding A Shikshamitra working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light around 5 PM on Saturday. According to reports, the school peon found him hanging from a noose in a classroom and immediately alerted the family and police. 3. UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy; mentor’s roots traced to Barabanki After reports of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s death, a village in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, has drawn attention for its historical link to Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khamenei. Residents of Kintur village claim Khamenei’s ancestors belonged to their village and were known in Iran as “Musavi Hindi.” Locals say several descendants later moved to Iran and contributed to religious and social developments there. 4. Mob attacks US embassy in Pak’s Karachi, 12 dead The United States and Israel continued airstrikes on Iran for the second consecutive day, intensifying tensions across the Middle East. Iran has reportedly retaliated with strikes targeting US military bases in Israel and across nine countries in the region. 5. Protests in Lucknow after Khamenei’s death; Shia community raises slogans Following the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests erupted in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community took to the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests as protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel.” 6. Attackers flee to Delhi after slitting YouTuber Saleem Wastik’s throat YouTuber Saleem Wastik from Loni on the Delhi-Ghaziabad border is battling for his life after two unidentified attackers entered his house and slit his throat. He is admitted to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital in Delhi with multiple knife wounds and remains in critical condition. CCTV footage tracked the attackers for about 2.5 km before they fled towards Delhi. 7. 17 killed in blast at Nagpur's detonator manufacturing company A massive explosion occurred on Sunday, 1 March 2026, at SBL Energy Limited, an ammunition manufacturing company located in Raulgaon, Katol taluka of Nagpur, Maharashtra. In this explosion, 17 workers were killed, and 18 were injured. Many of the injured are in critical condition. 8. 7-year-old Vaishnavi dies of burns in Lucknow; village mourns A wave of grief swept a Barabanki village after seven-year-old Vaishnavi, who had suffered 60% burns, died after a week at Lucknow’s trauma centre. Just days before Holi, her body was brought home for the last rites. Villagers gathered in the narrow lanes in tears, praying that no family should face such tragedy. 9. March likely to bring intense heat wave; temperature may touch 40°C Winter officially ends on March 1, but this year rising temperatures are already raising concerns. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), March could be among the warmest months on record, with temperatures in Uttar Pradesh likely to touch 40°C and the summer expected to be harsher than last year. 10. Banks will not operate for 18 days in March 2026 In March 2026, banks will not operate for a total of 18 days in different states across the country. According to the calendar issued by the RBI, banks will remain closed for 11 days at different locations next month, in addition to 5 Sundays and the second and fourth Saturdays.

stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her husband in Kanpur, who strangled her to death and dumped the body in a drain to destroy evidence. According to police, the accused wrapped the body of his wife, Akriti Singh alias Ruby, in a blanket and threw it into a drain located about 500 metres from their house in Saraimeeta area of Panki. He also placed stones on the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body spotted in drain, police informed The incident came to light on Saturday morning when passersby noticed a human head in the drain and immediately alerted the police. Officers reached the spot, recovered the body and sent it to the mortuary for post-mortem examination. Later that night, Akriti’s brother identified the body and confirmed her identity to the police. See 2 images- Love marriage five years ago Police said Akriti had married the accused in a temple five years ago after a love relationship. The couple had been living together in the Panki area since then. Initial investigation suggests there were ongoing domestic disputes between the couple, which eventually led to the murder. Husband and two relatives arrested Police have arrested the accused husband along with his two brothers, who are suspected of helping him dispose of the body. All three are currently being interrogated. During questioning, the husband confessed to strangling his wife. CCTV footage deleted to hide evidence Investigators also discovered that CCTV footage from the house had been deliberately deleted in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence and mislead the investigation. Police said further questioning and forensic examination are underway, and additional legal action will follow based on the findings. Frequent fights over jewellery worth lakhs, says victim’s brother The victim’s brother said Akriti had married Nitin of her own choice five years ago, and the family had supported the marriage. She regularly visited her maternal home, where their mother had given her jewellery worth several lakhs. According to the brother, Akriti would wear the jewellery during family functions but would later return it to her maternal home for safekeeping. However, her husband Nitin often objected to this and insisted she bring the jewellery back with her. When Akriti refused, he would question her decision. She reportedly told him she feared he might sell the jewellery and spend the money, which led to frequent arguments between the couple. Police mediation on February 26, murder committed after returning home The brother further revealed that Nitin had assaulted Akriti on February 26. Following the assault, Akriti approached the Panki Temple police post and filed a complaint. Police called both Akriti and Nitin to the police post and facilitated a compromise between them. After the mediation, the couple returned home. However, later that same day, Nitin allegedly assaulted Akriti again. He then strangled her to death, wrapped her body in a blanket, and dumped it in a drain located about 500 metres from their house. He also placed stones over the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body found in drain, police alerted by passersby On the morning of February 28, passersby noticed a body in the drain and immediately informed police by calling the emergency helpline number 112. Police from Panki police station reached the spot and recovered the body. Initial attempts to identify the victim were unsuccessful, and the body was sent to the mortuary. Later, family members identified the deceased as Akriti Singh alias Ruby, after which police intensified the investigation and arrested the accused husband and his relatives. Police conducting postmortem today Late Saturday night when family members got information about the incident through social media, they contacted Panki police. When police showed the photo to brother Rahul, he identified the body as his sister Akriti Singh aka Ruby. Today on Sunday, police are conducting the postmortem. After postmortem, police will hand over the body to Akriti's family. Then the last rites will be performed. Husband Confessed - Murdered by Strangulation Police arrested the accused husband Nitin Savita, brother-in-law Deepu and Rahul late Saturday night. Father-in-law Suresh Master was also taken into custody but was released due to poor health. DCP MS Kasim Abdi said- The accused are being interrogated. The accused husband has confessed to murdering by strangulation and disposing of the body. Accused Deleted Home CCTV Footage DCP said - Action will be taken based on the complaint from the maternal family. How did he take the body from house to drain? Did anyone else help in this? What was the main reason for murder... investigation is ongoing on these and other points. The accused has deleted the footage from home CCTV cameras. Footage from other nearby cameras is being examined.

stories.title: Boyfriend Ends Life After Girlfriend’s Death in UP's Sultanpur:Leaves note saying 'life meaningless without her'; couple buried together
stories.summary: A lover committed suicide after his girlfriend's death in UP's Sultanpur. Both were in a relationship for 3 years. The girlfriend died in a road accident on the afternoon of February 25. Upon hearing the news, the young man was heartbroken. He reached her home to see her one last time and learned that she had been buried. The young man named Vineet went straight to the cemetery. He started digging the grave. When people present there stopped him, he left and never returned. Two days later, on February 28, his body was found hanging in a garden. The family buried him near his girlfriend's grave. Meanwhile, Vineet's Instagram post has come into light. It said “Hello brothers this is my last video. What will I live for now when my life is no longer in this world. Please forgive me brothers, bye". Understand entire step by step sequence of events Vineet (25), a resident of Ghatampur, was the youngest of three brothers. He had studied till fourth grade. His father died 5 years ago. He met Arpita in a clothing store where they both used to work and gradually fell in love. According to Vineet's brother Swamitt, Arpita died in a road accident on February 25. She had gone to the market with her brother, where a car hit their bike. Swamitt said “When Vineet learned about Arpita's death the next day, he was shocked. He went to her house to see Arpita for the last time. There he fainted while crying. Then we brought him back home”. Vineet was very disturbed after Arpita's death According to Vineet's sister in law Kajal “He was very disturbed since Arpita's death and stopped eating and drinking. He wasn't talking to anyone. He went there again in the evening. Found out that she had been buried. After this, he went to Arpita's grave where he started digging her grave”. She further added “When people stopped him, he ran away. Then he didn't return. He was searched extensively but couldn't be found. After this, we filed a missing person report for Vineet at the police station”. Police found Vineet's location in a garden After the filing of missing report police searched for Vineet for two days but couldn't find him. Police tried to trace his phone where his location was found in a garden 8 km away from the village. When family members and police reached there, they found his body hanging. Police found a love letter from his pocket Police lowered the body and searched the surroundings. Police also found a love letter from his pocket. After this, the body was sent for post-mortem. On Saturday evening, after the post-mortem, the body came home and family members performed the last rites and his body was buried right next to Arpita's grave.

stories.title: How a UP village shaped Khamenei’s legacy:Supreme Leader's mentor had roots in Barabanki, known as 'Musavi Hindi' in Iran
stories.summary: After reports of the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district has come into the spotlight due to its claimed historical connection with Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini. Residents of Kintur village say that the ancestors of Ruhollah Khomeini, who led Iran’s 1979 Islamic Revolution, belonged to their village. Locals claim that several descendants of this village later went to Iran and played a role in religious and social developments there. According to villagers, people from Barabanki used to travel to Iran on religious pilgrimages during the time of the Nawabs. They also say that Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, lived in Kintur village during the 18th and early 19th centuries before moving abroad. Following the news of Khamenei’s death, Syed Nihal Miyan, who claims to be a descendant of Khomeini and lives in Kintur, expressed deep sorrow. He said Khamenei stood for humanity beyond religion and community, and his death was a great loss. Another local resident, Dr Rehan Kazmi, described Khamenei’s death in the Israeli attack as “martyrdom” and called it an irreparable loss. Khomeini’s grandfather had roots in Barabanki According to local accounts and historical references, Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, was born in Kintur village in the early 19th century. The village has long been known as a centre of Shia Islamic learning. In 1830, Syed Ahmad Musavi left British India on a religious journey to Najaf, a major Shia religious centre in present-day Iraq. He later settled in Najaf and eventually moved to the Iranian city of Khomein. To preserve his Indian identity, he added the word “Hindi” to his name and became known as Syed Ahmad Musavi Hindi. Iranian records still mention this name. He later bought a house in Iran and married Sakineh. The couple had four children, including a son whose descendants later included Ruhollah Khomeini, the architect of Iran’s Islamic Revolution. Today, residents of Kintur village say this historical link remains a matter of pride and has once again drawn attention after the reported death of Iran’s Supreme Leader. Religious influence and heritage linked to Musavi family The Musavi family, to which Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini belonged, is believed to be descended from the seventh Shia Imam, Imam Musa al-Kazim. Because of this lineage, the family held a respected position in Shia religious circles and was known for its spiritual leadership. Syed Ahmad Musavi, Khomeini’s grandfather, played an important role in preserving this religious legacy. He later settled in the Middle East and died in Karbala in 1869. His teachings and ideology continued to influence his family and future generations, including Ruhollah Khomeini. Even today, villagers in Kintur claim that descendants of Khomeini’s family continue to live in the ancestral house in Barabanki, maintaining the historical and cultural connection between the village and Iran. The Iranian revolution of 1979 and Khomeini’s leadership In 1979, Ruhollah Khomeini led the Islamic Revolution in Iran, which ended the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and established Iran as an Islamic Republic. Following the revolution, Khomeini became the country’s Supreme Leader. Despite holding the highest position of power, Khomeini was known for his simple lifestyle. He lived in a modest single-storey house and reportedly avoided using public funds for personal comfort. His leadership and ideology played a major role in shaping modern Iran’s political and religious structure. Rise of Ali Khamenei after Khomeini’s death Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was born on July 17, 1939, in Mashhad, Iran. Inspired by Khomeini’s teachings, he actively participated in the Islamic Revolution and became one of Khomeini’s trusted associates. After Khomeini’s death in 1989, Khamenei was appointed as Iran’s Supreme Leader. He remained in this position for decades, becoming one of the most influential figures in Iran’s political and religious system. While Khamenei himself did not have direct links with India, his mentor Khomeini’s ancestral roots in Uttar Pradesh have continued to attract attention. Historical importance of Kintur village in Barabanki Kintur village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district holds historical significance due to its claimed connection with Syed Ahmad Musavi. From this village, Musavi travelled abroad and eventually settled in Iran, where his descendants went on to influence the country’s history. Several Shia families in the village still recall their ancestral links to Iran. Syed Nihal Kazmi, a 70-year-old resident, claims that his great-grandfather, Mufti Mohammad Quli Musavi, and Syed Ahmad Musavi were cousins. Locals say this connection remains an important part of the village’s identity, and recent developments in Iran have once again brought attention to Kintur’s historical and religious heritage.

stories.title: Lord Krishna plays Holi in Mathura's Gokul:Rides in a palaki from Nand Bhavan to Murlighat, chants of 'Jai Radhe Jai Krishna' echoes.
stories.summary: The atmosphere has turned festive in Braj with people immersed in celebration of Holi with their beloved Lord Krishna. Folk songs are being sung in every home and the temples are echoing with the chants of “Jai Radhe Jai Krishna”. On Sunday (March 1st), people gathered to celebrate Holi with Lord Krishna's form in Gokul. They have brought abir, colors and sticks with them and are accompanied by their family members and friends. Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ marking the beginning of the festivities The palaki ride emerged from Nand Bhavan, where Lord Krishna in his child form was seated in his palaki. From here the palaki reached to Murlidhar Ghat where it is believed that Lord played flute for the first time. At the ghat Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ (Holi with sticks) with the Gopis, marking the beginning of Holi celebrations in Gokul. ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ is celebrated in memory of Lord Krishna's childhood form and his divine plays. This festival is specially celebrated keeping the image of ‘Bal Gopal’ (child form of Lord Krishna) at the center. Therefore, small sticks called ‘Chhari’ are used instead of large sticks called ‘Lath’.

stories.title: ‘Only death will free me from SIR’:BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; wrote he was denied leave for daughter’s wedding
stories.summary: A Shikshamitra, who was working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur, allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light on Saturday evening around 5 PM. According to information, the school peon saw the teacher hanging from a noose inside a classroom. He immediately raised an alarm and informed the family members as well as the police. Police reached the school soon after. The classroom door was open, and the teacher was found hanging inside. He was taken down and rushed to a nearby hospital, but doctors declared him dead. During the initial investigation, police found a suicide note kept on the teacher’s table. Further inquiry is underway.. It read: I am fed up with work. My daughter's wedding is on March 8th. I am not getting leave. That's why I am committing suicide. After dying, I will be free from SIR. After the teacher's death, villagers and family members created a ruckus at the hospital. Upon receiving this information, officials arrived and somehow pacified the family. After this, the body was sent for a post-mortem. The case is from the Bindki Kotwali area. ADM Avinash Tripathi stated: The suicide note that was found will be investigated. Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report is received. First, read the BLO's suicide note I, Akhilesh Kumar, am fed up with the BLO's work. For this work, I made rounds of officers, SDM and EO sir. My daughter is getting married. I said that someone else should be assigned the duty, but no officer or employee was willing to listen. The event is on March 8. Despite having so much work, I am continuously doing the BLO's work. My household chores remained incomplete. How much work can I, a single person, do? Distressed by this, I have been forced to take my own life. The Election Commission is responsible for me and my family. After my death, I will be freed from SIR. Taught children all day, found hanging in the evening In Aliabad village, Akhilesh Savita (50) lived with his wife Manju Devi, daughter Divyanshi (20), and son Divyansh. Akhilesh was a Shikshamitra (para-teacher) at the village's primary school. He was deployed for BLO work in SIR. His daughter Divyanshi's wedding was scheduled for March 8. He was asking for leave for this. It is alleged that he was not getting leave. On Saturday, he reached school at 9 AM. He taught the children. The children were dismissed at 3 PM. After this, he started doing SIR work. The other teachers went to their respective homes. The school peon arrived at 5 PM. He saw the teacher's body hanging. He called the family and the police. The family took him to Bindki CHC, where doctors declared him dead. Family members protested for 4 hours Villagers and family members started shouting slogans against the district administration. Upon receiving information about the incident, Bindki DSP Gaurav Sharma reached the CHC with the Kotwali police force. Officials pacified the family for 4 hours. After this, the family members finally agreed. Police sent the body for post-mortem. After the post-mortem, family members loaded the body into a car and took it to the village. Akhilesh's brother Bhupesh Kumar said- My brother was worried about leave for several weeks for his daughter's wedding. I myself went for leave, but he committed suicide because he didn't get it.

stories.title: UP on high alert as Shia protests erupt over Khamenei:People take to streets; gulf flights cancelled across region
stories.summary: After the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests have begun in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community came out onto the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests. Protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel”. A woman shouted- Those who have treachery in their blood have killed Khamenei through deception. Khamenei was my lion. If one Khamenei is killed, thousands of Khameneis will rise... Israel and America are deceivers. The All India Shia Personal Law Board has announced three days of mourning. The board’s general secretary, Maulana Yasoob Abbas, said people will put up black flags at their homes and wear black clothes. Religious gatherings will be organised in Khamenei’s name. A large crowd gathered outside Jamia Millia Islamia in southeast Delhi, where people assembled to offer prayers at a nearby mosque following reports of the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in a joint U.S.–Israel strike. The gathering witnessed people expressing grief and solidarity, while groups of students and local community leaders also staged a protest, raising slogans and voicing support for the late Iranian leader.
