stories.title: UP Shia community stages state-wide protest over Ayatollah Khamenei's death:Lucknow witnesses biggest turnout as protestors take out march
stories.summary: Members of the Shia community staged large-scale protests across Uttar Pradesh on Sunday following reports of the death of following the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The demonstrations were marked by candle marches, sloganeering and traditional mourning rituals. Massive turnout in Lucknow In Lucknow, nearly one lakh people gathered late Sunday night to protest. A candle march was taken out from Chota Imambara to Bara Imambara. Protesters carried posters of Khamenei and raised slogans against the United States and Israel. In several cities, effigies of the United States were burnt. Processions were also held in Bijnor and Amroha, where members of the Shia community marched in large numbers. Mourning rituals similar to Muharram In scenes reminiscent of Muharram observances, youths and children engaged in self-flagellation using chains as a mark of grief. Mourning processions were also reported in Prayagraj, where women organised candle marches. Earlier in the day, as news of Khamenei’s death spread, expressions of grief and anger began surfacing. Protesters said their leader’s “martyrdom” would not go unanswered. The All India Shia Personal Law Board announced three days of mourning. Its General Secretary, Maulana Yasoob Abbas, said people would hoist black flags atop their homes and wear black clothing. Both Chota Imambara and Bara Imambara will remain closed until March 3. Political reactions and security alert Reacting to the protests, BJP MLA Rajeshwar Singh condemned the demonstrations related to Iran. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan from Moradabad urged people not to lose control in the heat of the moment. Amid the statewide protests, police have issued a high alert across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also held a meeting with senior officials on Sunday morning, directing them to exercise caution and maintain law and order. Authorities continue to monitor the situation closely to prevent any untoward incidents.

stories.title: Son kills mother-father, sister and grandmother in Bahraich:Accused kept hitting with an axe for 30 mins; brother's condition critical
stories.summary: A young man killed his parents, sister and grandmother in UP's Bahraich. He continuously attacked the family with an axe for 30 minutes. He also tried to kill his elder brother, who came to intervene, but somehow he survived. A 10-year-old nephew watched the entire incident while hiding. When villagers rushed to the spot after hearing screams, they were stunned by the scene. Bodies were lying on the floor and the bed. The elder brother was groaning in pain. Seeing people, the accused tried to commit suicide. He hit his head several times with a brick. He fell unconscious due to excessive bleeding. Police arrived on information. The accused was arrested and sent to the district hospital. Due to his critical condition, he was referred to Lucknow Trauma Centre. It is being reported that there was a long-running property dispute between the two brothers for many years. Late at night, an argument broke out between the two over this dispute. During this, in anger, the young man attacked the entire family with an axe. Currently, the forensic team has recovered the axe used in the attack. Police are investigating the case. The incident took place in Ramnagar Basantpur Udal village of Rupaideeha police station area, 45 kilometres away from the district headquarters. 10-year-old innocent witnessed the scene of death The only eyewitness to the incident, Gurudev's 10-year-old son Azad, narrowly escaped. He was with his father in another room at the time of the incident. Hearing the commotion, he came out. Upon seeing his uncle, he hid outside. He watched the entire murder unfold before his eyes. Currently, the police have taken Azad into their protection. They are gathering information from him about the incident. Gurudev Verma has filed a written complaint against Nirankar at Rupaideeha police station. Police have arrested Nirankar and sent him to Lucknow for treatment. Detailed interrogation will be conducted once he recovers. Family was about to leave for Gonda in just a few hours Neighbours said that Gurdev's entire family were followers of 'Jai Gurudev'. The whole family was supposed to leave on Monday morning for the Jai Gurudev gathering in Gonda. The deceased Parvati had also arrived at her parents' home from her in-laws' house on Sunday morning to go to Gonda with the family. Parvati was married to Pappu Verma in Lokhariyan Purwa village under the Malhipur police station area of Shravasti. They have two children. Land division and old transactions People reported - The family owned approximately 18 bigha of agricultural land. Both brothers farmed by dividing it equally between themselves. An open conflict between them had never surfaced before. About 15 years ago, their father had sold 12 biswa of land in Thanahi village. With that money, some land was purchased in the village. Initial investigation suggests the dispute may be related to the distribution of land and money. Two years ago, the accused's wife had left him Police said - Questioning of neighbours revealed that the accused Nirankar was married about seven years ago in Birpur village of Rupaideeha police station area. According to family members, his wife left home about two years after marriage. They have no children. He had been under mental stress since his wife left. Forensic team collected evidence, force deployed in village - ASP ASP (Rural) Durga Prasad Tiwari said- Initial investigation reveals a land dispute case. Forensic team is present at the spot. Treatment of the accused is ongoing. The axe used in the incident was recovered from near the bushes. All four bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Heavy police force has been deployed in the village to deal with any untoward situation. Village shocked before Holi, family plunged into mourning This mass murder just before Holi has shaken the entire village. The atmosphere is gloomy with four funeral processions from a single house. Police claim that law and order are normal, but additional forces have been deployed as a precaution.

stories.title: Prayagraj families struggle as loved ones stuck in Iran:Tensions erupt amid escalating conflict and flight suspensions
stories.summary: Many people from Prayagraj are currently caught in the escalating conflict between Iran and Israel, leaving families anxious about the safety of their loved ones. While some manage to check in through video calls, others are unable to communicate at all. The family of SP leader Dan Bahadur from Jhunsi is stranded in Israel. Dan Bahadur Singh said he recently spoke to his children via video call. His daughter told him, “Papa, sirens go off due to missile attack threats, and we run to bunkers. We are safe for now.” His daughter Kavita, son-in-law Rajesh Yadav, and one-year-old grandson Ritvik have been living in Israel for about four years, where Rajesh works as a research scholar. Sister and family stranded in Iran Syed Mohammad Askari’s sister, her husband, and their son are stranded in Iran. They live in Qom, where his sister teaches at a madrasa. The brother-in-law hails from Karari in Kaushambi. The family has been settled in Iran for around 35 years. No contact since February 18 Askari said the last communication was on February 18. Normally, they would speak every 8–10 days, but since the attacks began, all contact has been lost. Calls go unanswered. Sakib from Daryabad also stuck in Iran Sakib Mustafa, son of Khushnoor Raja Rizvi from Daryabad, is also in Iran. Rizvi said they spoke a day before the attacks began, but have not been able to reach him since. The family continues trying, but network and security restrictions prevent communication.

stories.title: Akshat played Ravan in Ramleela, wrote his own scripts:Now accused of killing father and weaving false story in Lucknow murder case
stories.summary: A new revelation has emerged in the murder case of the owner of a well-known pathology lab in Lucknow. It is being said that Akshat Pratap Singh alias Raja, the son who murdered Manvendra Singh, the owner of Vardhman Pathology, is skilled in scriptwriting. He used to prepare the entire script for the Ramlila held in the colony. He also selected the characters himself. He himself played the roles of Ravana and Parshuram. Recently, a video of him acting in Ramlila has surfaced. Local residents say that Akshat was an excellent scriptwriter. This is why he easily misled the police. He fabricated a false story from the murder to disposing of the body. He did it so meticulously that everyone was forced to believe it was true. Based on this, the police stated that the dispute over NEET exam preparation was the reason for the murder. However, the family and neighbors are not satisfied with this revelation by the police. They believe that the dispute over NEET preparation alone cannot be the reason behind the murder. It is reported that on February 20, Akshat shot his sleeping father in the head with a licensed rifle at 4:30 AM. He bought a saw and a blue drum. In the bathroom, he dismembered the hands and feet with the saw. He put them in a polythene bag and threw them about 20 kilometers away in Sadrauna, Kakori. He tried to cut the torso into two pieces but couldn't. He filled it in the drum. He bought 10 liters of turpentine oil to burn the remaining body. He was planning to take the torso far away and burn it, but he was caught before that. While writing the script for Ramleela, he wrote the story of his father's murder The people of the neighborhood said - Akshat used to prepare the entire script of Ramlila with a boy from the neighborhood. Who would do what? He also decided this. He used to start this work a month in advance. People said - Akshat used to play all the angry characters in Ramlila. During this, he would get immersed in his role. Meanwhile, a video of Akshat during his portrayal of Parshuram also surfaced, in which he is conversing with Lakshman after breaking the bow. It shows that Akshat is completely immersed in his character. People sitting nearby are watching with great enthusiasm. The committee and the people of the neighborhood say - while playing Ramlila characters, everyone used to say that Akshat is very skilled, every child should play a role like him. However, now everyone wants their child to stay miles away from Akshat's shadow. Police are scanning mobile data Police sources said that the data from Akshat and Manvendra Singh's mobiles is being scanned. Their call details, messages, as well as WhatsApp and social media are also being investigated. Police hope that this may yield some important evidence. Bank accounts are also being investigated Police sources said - the bank account details of accused Akshat and Manvendra are also being scrutinized. stories.title: Yogi Adityanath commences 4-day Gorakhpur visit with RSS coordination meeting:Will review development projects before joining Holi celebrations
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath reached Gorakhpur on Monday morning for a four-day visit. He arrived at the Circuit House by helicopter and then proceeded to the Annexe building, where he held a coordination meeting with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) officials. The two-hour meeting was attended by BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary, vice-president Dr Dharmendra Singh, and regional president Sahajanand Rai. The Chief Minister discussed preparations for the RSS centenary year ceremony and programmes planned for Chaitra Navratri. He invited suggestions from RSS functionaries to improve governance and public welfare, and several officials shared their inputs. RSS provincial pracharak Ramesh, provincial sanghchalak Dr. Mahendra Agrawal, and other office-bearers were also present at the meeting. After the meeting, the Chief Minister visited Gorakhnath Temple, where he offered prayers to Guru Gorakhnath. He then paid respects at the Memorial of Brahmleen Mahant Avedyanath and reviewed development works and Holi preparations with officials. In the evening, he will participate in the Bhakt Prahlad procession organised under the Shri Shri Holika Dahan Utsav Samiti.

stories.title: Priest to walk through raging flames of Holika pyre:Braj's Prahlad temple to start a 45-day ritual to celebrate the occasion
stories.summary: Amidst the 45-day Holi celebration of Braj, a shocking sight is seen in Phalen village here. Here, a 'Panda' (priest/devotee) runs through the blazing embers of a Holika pyre, spread across 20 feet in length and 30 feet in width. The Panda does not get burned even a little in the fire. This tradition has been observed in Phalen village since Satya Yuga. Sanju, from the Panda family, has been observing celibacy and performing fasts and rituals for 45 days in the temple of devotee Prahlad. Before this, he circumambulated the entire village. The village is being decorated for the Panda fair. Houses are being painted and whitewashed. More than 50,000 tourists visit the village to witness this 5300-year-old tradition. How does the Panda emerge from the Holika fire? Why doesn't he burn in the fire? What is the belief behind this tradition? Is it being performed by members of the same family? To know all this, Dainik Bhaskar's team reached Phalen village in Chhata tehsil, 50 km away from Mathura district headquarters. Read the report First, let's know the atmosphere of Phalen village Phalen village has a population of about 10,000. There is an atmosphere of enthusiasm here. The village is being decorated and beautified. Cleaning is underway. Villagers are painting and whitewashing their houses. They are painting the doors. Temples and houses are being decorated with colorful lighting. Tulsiram, who paints houses, said - At Panna Mela, we decorate the village like this. We do cleaning. This is our festival. Charan Singh says that preparations like Diwali are made here for Holi. Houses are painted and whitewashed, and dishes are prepared for the arriving guests. Village head Kailash said that he is running a cleanliness drive. Prahlad Kund has been cleaned. Talking to people, it became clear that this village is famous for 2 reasons Understand what kind of fast the Panda observes Sanju Panda is observing a fast in Prahlad Temple We asked the villagers where the Panda was and what kind of fast he observes? The villagers took us to Prahlad's temple located outside the village. A person was sitting in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple. He was chanting with a rosary. People told us that this is Sanju Panda. On the day of Holika Dahan, late Monday night, he will emerge from the blazing Holika amidst its flames. He will do this for the second time. To witness the Panda safely emerging from the burning Holika, people arrive not only from India but also from abroad. The villagers said that their family members have been coming out from the middle of the burning Holika for 5300 years. In this way, they bring to life the mythological story of Prahlada, son of Hiranyakashipu, surviving and Holika being burnt to ashes in Satya Yuga. Sanju Panda has been chanting in this temple for 45 days. What is his daily routine during his fast? What rules does he follow. Sanjoo Panda to Emerge from Holika Dahan for the Second Time Sanjoo Panda, a resident of Phalen village, will emerge from the burning fire of Holi for the second time this year. Before this, his brother Monu Panda has emerged 4 times and his father Sushil 8 times. Sanjoo Panda says that his family has been observing this tradition since the Satya Yuga. He claims that in this very village, Holika sat with devotee Prahlad in her lap. But not even a hair of Prahlad, the devout devotee of Lord Narayan, was harmed. Holika was burnt to ashes. Sanjoo Panda says that preparations for this begin from Basant Panchami. For this, I observe a fast for one and a quarter months (45 days). They stay at the temple, separate from home. During the fast, they consume only fruits once a day. They can drink only as much water as fits in the palm of their hand at one time. They do not go outside the village. They sleep on a bed laid on the ground. They observe celibacy. He says- one who observes this fast never catches the tail of a cow. Never uses items made of leather. It feels as if Prahlada Dev himself is with us. My elder brother Monu Panda has been observing the tradition of emerging from the burning Holika since 2020. Monu said that Sanju is chanting with the rosary for 6-6 hours Sanju's brother Monu Panda said that hundreds of years ago, a rosary appeared from the Prahlad Kund of the village. This rosary remains in the temple. It is believed that this very rosary was around Prahlad ji's neck. This rosary had 7 large beads (small round objects, which are strung together with a thread to make a rosary). Later, Mauni Baba prepared a rosary of 108 beads from these seven beads. Monu says- Many generations chant with this rosary for a month. On the day of Holika Dahan, only after bathing in Prahlad Kund and wearing this rosary, are they able to pass through the flames. My brother Sanju chants with this rosary for 6 hours each in the morning and evening. Havan begins 24 hours earlier Sanju Panda's father, Sushil Panda, said that Dhamaar singing begins 36 hours before emerging from the Holi fire. While the Havan (fire ritual) is started 24 hours earlier. When the fire of this Havan starts to subside, only then is the Holi pyre lit, and the Panda emerges from the temple and bathes directly in the Kund (pond). Then he emerges from the burning fire of Holi. Sushil Panda claims that when he emerges from the fire, Lord Prahlad, in the form of a child, walks ahead of him, due to which the fire is not felt at all. Collective Holi of 12 Villages is Lit Prahlad Kund is located near Lord Prahlad's temple in Phalain village. The collective Holi of 12 villages is lit near this Kund. In this, cow dung cakes are contributed from every house in the villages of Phalain, Paigaon, Supana, Rajgarhi Bhikhgarhi Nagla Mew, Mehroli, Vishambhara, Rohita 3 Bisa, 7 Bisa, 10 Bisa, and Chonkarwas. Additionally, the village head orders Jharberia wood from Rajasthan. This is the form of Holi Charan Singh, a resident of Phalain, says that Holi here is 20 feet high and 30 feet in diameter. When this Holi burns, its flames are so intense that people living nearby cannot even stand. Charan Singh says all this is possible only by the grace of Lord Narayan and devotee Prahlad ji. Understand the process of Holika Puja Panda will bathe, sister will offer oblation to the fire Idols of Prahlad emerged from the ground The people of the village believe that the idols in Prahladji's temple emerged from the ground. It is believed that centuries ago, a saint came to Phalen village. Here, he found idols of devotee Prahlad and Lord Narasimha under a tree. The saint gave these idols to the Punda family of the village. After which the saint said- Install these idols in the temple. Worship them. Every year, on the festival of Holika, a member of this family should pass through the burning fire. He gave a boon that the burning fire of Holi would not harm them. Since then, this tradition has been going on. Why doesn't the Punda burn in the fire? We tried to understand this in two ways. The first fact is what the Punda family believes. The second fact is what science says. Self-power increases with fasting, heat is felt, but they don't burn According to the Punda family, self-power increases with a 45-day fast before running on fire. Additionally, Prahlada's garland protects them from burning in the fire. While running with a wet body, the heat of the fire is felt, but the body does not burn. BHU Professor Says - No Such Rule in Physics Professor Ajay Tyagi of BHU's Physics Department says - There is no rule in science that an ordinary person can run through blazing fire and remain unharmed. It is possible that he (the priest) applies something to his body before going into the fire. It is also possible that he applies something to his body or it could be some trick.

stories.title: Faecal bacteria found in UP bottled water units:164 plants shut, 80% fail safety standards in Statewide inspection
stories.summary: If you regularly consume bottled water believing it to be safe, these findings raise serious concerns. A statewide inspection by the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) found that nearly 80% of packaged drinking water and mineral water units in Uttar Pradesh failed to meet safety standards. Several plants showed poor maintenance, while others had microbial contamination, including bacteria that indicate faecal presence. The special inspection drive was launched under the direction of FSDA Commissioner Roshan Jacob, with teams from different divisions sent to inspect units across the state. The campaign revealed large-scale deficiencies, leading to suspension of licences and shutdown of several plants. 850 licensed units in UP, 560 inspected during special drive According to Joint Food Commissioner Harishankar Singh, Uttar Pradesh has licences for around 850 packaged drinking water units. Out of these, 560 units were inspected as part of the special statewide campaign. Water samples were collected from 397 plants and sent for laboratory testing. The results showed that 194 plants failed to meet prescribed quality standards. Only 84 units were found fully compliant, meaning nearly 79% of tested plants did not meet safety norms. Faecal contamination bacteria found in 119 plants Laboratory testing detected Escherichia coli and coliform bacteria in samples from 119 plants. The presence of these bacteria indicates possible contamination from faecal matter, including human or animal waste. Officials warned that such contamination poses serious health risks and can lead to multiple diseases. In addition to microbial growth, some plants were found to have excess mineral content and other quality deficiencies. 164 licences suspended, over 100 units issued improvement notices Following the inspection findings, authorities took strict action. Licences of 164 packaged drinking water units were suspended immediately, and these plants were shut down. In addition, 104 units were issued notices directing them to rectify deficiencies and improve their facilities to meet safety standards. Officials said packaged drinking water has been categorised as a high-risk food product, prompting stricter monitoring and enforcement. Earlier BIS certification mandatory, now only FSSAI licence required Previously, setting up a packaged drinking water unit required certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), along with a licence from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). BIS certification involved inspection of water sources, processing systems, and laboratory facilities before granting approval. However, from October 17, 2024, BIS certification is no longer mandatory. Only an FSSAI licence is now required to operate such units. Under FSSAI norms, regular testing remains compulsory, including monthly microbiological testing, chemical testing every three months, and source water testing every six months to ensure safety. Statewide campaign exposes widespread violations The special inspection campaign exposed significant lapses in safety and quality across packaged drinking water units in Uttar Pradesh. The findings have raised serious concerns about regulatory compliance and public health, prompting authorities to tighten monitoring and enforcement across the sector. Diseases can occur when coliform bacteria are excessive Dr. A.Q. Jilani at Lohia Medical Institute explains that while it is normal to find coliform bacteria in water generally. However, when present in excessive amounts, it can lead to many diseases. These bacteria can cause various illnesses in the stomach or lower abdominal region. In Lucknow, Additional Commissioner Food Vijay Pratap Singh explains that obtaining a license for packaged drinking water or mineral water plant is a lengthy process. For this, one needs to apply for a license on FSSAI's website FOSCOS. The instructions given there must be followed.

stories.title: Gopis playfully strike with sticks, Krishna urges them on:Flowers and colours rain down in Gokul’s Lathmar Holi
stories.summary: In Gokul, the city of Lord Krishna, on Sunday, gopis dressed like brides applied color to the child forms of Lord Krishna and Balaram. Then, they showered sticks wrapped in brocade cloth on the revelers (huriyare) dressed as Kanha. Even the policemen on security duty could not escape these sticks. In fact, the tradition of Chhadimar Holi in Gokul is centuries old. According to mythological belief, child Krishna used to tease the gopis of Gokul by stealing butter and playing pranks. Angered by this, the gopis would chase him with sticks. This Holi, played with a feeling of love and affection, makes this tradition unique and special compared to other places.

stories.title: Yogi pulls up police over assault on 'Batuk':Says no repeat complaint after constable pulled hair at Kashi Vishwanath temple
stories.summary: CM Yogi is on a 2-day visit to Varanasi. On the first day, Sunday, he held a meeting at the Circuit House. During this, he reprimanded officials regarding the assault on a Batuk at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Expressing displeasure, he said that the police should not misbehave with devotees. There should also be no complaints of mismanagement here. Actually, on February 27, a constable beat up a Batuk at the gate of Baba Vishwanath Dham in Kashi. The constable slapped him 3 times. Then the sub-inspector pulled his hair and pushed him behind the barricading. He was not allowed to join the queue. Yogi said - Police should improve their working style On Sunday, he reviewed development works, construction projects, and law and order in the Circuit House auditorium. He said that the temple administration should improve the arrangements, so that devotees coming here do not face any difficulty. At the same time, the police should also improve. He said that such complaints should not be received in the future. Any kind of negligence regarding crime will not be tolerated. No leniency will be shown towards criminals. The CM also reviewed the upcoming festivals. He said that action should be taken against those who create nuisance during Holi. For festivals to conclude peacefully, police and administration officials should remain vigilant 24 hours a day. The CM said that arrangements should be made for devotees to reach the shops built in the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. The prices of materials available in the temple should be fair. Religious institutions are not a means to earn money, but places of devotion, therefore, better arrangements should be made at these places for devotees. CM said - Take action against those responsible for Codine cough syrup Yogi said that by increasing manpower, speed up the construction work of Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghat. During construction work near ghats and temples, historical heritage should be preserved in every situation. No new tradition should be allowed. Action should be taken against those using loud silencers and pressure horns. Vehicles should not be parked by encroaching on roads. Action should be taken against such people. said that action should be taken against the real responsible people involved in the illegal trade of codeine cough syrup cases. There should be no sale of illegal and poisonous liquor anywhere. Keep a close watch on the illegal transportation of liquor. Now read the full story of the Batuk incident Constable slapped, Sub-inspector pulled hair In Kashi, on February 27, on Rangbhari Ekadashi, Lord Shiva, along with Mother Parvati, arrived in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple in a palanquin. After the palanquin left, the police stopped the Batuks outside. The Batuks wanted to go inside, which led to an argument with the police. During this, a constable scratched Batuk's face and then started slapping him. The constable slapped him three times in quick succession, after which the sub-inspector pulled his hair, then dragged him out of the line. Despite waiting in line for hours, he could not gain entry. Policemen had abused a female journalist Misbehavior with a female journalist also came to light. Policemen on duty at Gate No. 4 misbehaved with the journalist. Another journalist who came to intervene was also slapped and chased away by the policemen, and they abused him. Then DCP Gaurav Banswal had said that the policemen seen in the video have been immediately removed from temple duty. They have been attached to the police line. Departmental inquiry is ongoing. .

stories.title: Ex-Muslim YouTuber attack accused dies in encounter:20 rounds fired, 2 policemen injured; inspector survives
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, on Sunday night, the assailant who stabbed YouTuber Salim Wastik 14 times was killed in an encounter. Loni police station in-charge narrowly escaped, a bullet hit his bulletproof jacket. While 2 other policemen were also shot. After the attack on the YouTuber, the police were searching for the attackers. During this, the police encountered the assailant in the Loni police station area. As soon as the police saw him, the bike-borne assailant started firing. About 20 rounds of firing took place from both sides for about 10 minutes. The assailant was injured after being shot in the chest. He died on the spot. While 2 policemen were shot in the arm. They are undergoing treatment at the district hospital. The deceased assailant has been identified as Zeeshan, a resident of Nagla Saifi, Amroha district. It was Zeeshan who attacked YouTuber Salim Wastik, who had left Islam, with a knife. A reward of one lakh rupees was declared on Zeeshan. See 3 pictures

stories.title: 'I saw Shankaracharya’s swimming pool myself', says writer:Claims building was not like an ashram; woman called herself Avimukteshwaranand’s close friend
stories.summary: Serious questions have been raised about the monastery linked to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. Writer Bhumika Dwivedi, who stayed there for two months, has claimed that the place does not function like a traditional ashram and that many mysteries are hidden inside the building. Bhumika Dwivedi said the building of Kashi Vidyapeeth is not an ashram in the true sense. She claimed she personally saw a swimming pool inside the premises. According to her, the students, known as batuks, were not allowed to speak to anyone. She said she did not see any ashram-like discipline during her stay. “There was no routine like morning bath, meditation or chanting,” she said. She added that the atmosphere did not reflect the spiritual environment normally associated with an ashram. Dwivedi also said that Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was not present during the time she stayed there. Because of this, she said she cannot comment on the allegations of sexual abuse involving the students. However, she claimed that in his absence, all powers were in the hands of a woman referred to as ‘Didi’. Recalling a conversation, Dwivedi said she once asked ‘Didi’ about her relationship with the Shankaracharya. “I asked her whether she was his mother, sister or relative. She smiled and said, ‘I am his friend.’ After that, I did not ask anything more,” Dwivedi said. She questioned what an ashram should be like. According to her, an ashram usually has simple surroundings, open ground and a disciplined life focused on prayer and study. In contrast, she described the monastery building as being made of marble and equipped with lifts, carpets and other luxury facilities. The investigation into the matter is still ongoing. Dwivedi said many secrets are yet to come out and that the truth will be revealed in time. Read the author's full interview Question- When did you stay at Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand's ashram? Author- I stayed at the ashram of Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand of Kashi from March 18, 2022 to May, 2022. At that time, there were 10-12 children there. All were children from villages and very poor families. There was a 'Didi' (elder sister/lady) who was considered the manager there. There was a manager, and some workers. A guest house is built in front of the ashram. It has very luxurious facilities. People can stay there, but no one can stay in the ashram. However, the 'Didi' (lady in charge) had two female relatives staying there. Question- What are the arrangements for studies in the ashram? Author- Vedic studies take place, but their discipline was not that strict. For example, one should wake up in the morning and bathe in Ganga water. One should recite the Gayatri Mantra and offer water to the sun. I wake up early in the morning. The children there did not wake up early in the morning. Nor were they encouraged to do yoga. There were no prayers or rituals performed early in the morning either. Question- With what purpose were you staying in Shankaracharya's ashram? Author- Writing...I wanted to write about Banaras, that's why I stayed in the ashram. Shankaracharya Swaroopanand has been a friend of my grandfather. He was like my grandfather. He said that I write on topics from all over the world. Why don't I write about Banaras? That's why I went there. Question - What all did you see in the ashram, please tell us? Writer. The ashram is very well built, the floor is marble, it is not built like a monastery with a raw mud floor. There are no flower beds there, there is no cowshed in the ashram, they say that a cowshed has been built somewhere far away. There wasn't a single cow there. Question- Have you seen any swimming pool with your own eyes? Author- Yes, I have definitely seen it. While staying there, I saw that a swimming pool was also built. I was told that the purpose for which it was built had been fulfilled. Therefore, it was not operational at that time. It is on the topmost floor. No one is allowed to go there. Question- Could anyone meet Shankaracharya? Author- Shankaracharya was not there at that time. But when he is in the ashram, no one could just meet him. Question- Did you observe any suspicious activity in the ashram? Author- No outsider can enter or exit many parts of the ashram. Entry is also restricted to the room where the Didi (mistress/owner) of the place lives. The splendid rooms she lives in are very luxurious. You could say that those living there have a secret life. There are many mysteries in that ashram. Even after so much commotion, no one can get entry to the roof. No one even reached that room. Question - Did you talk to any of the students (batuk) during your stay at the ashram? Writer - There, outsiders are kept very far from the students. They are not even allowed to talk. The students are also forbidden from talking to common people. Even with their parents, they are not allowed to talk much. Question- Who decides in the ashram who can meet Shankaracharya and the Batuks? Author- Didi and the manager decide who can come to the ashram? Who can they meet? Even the guardians who came could only meet for a short while. I think they do this so that parents don't develop too much attachment to the Batuks. Question- Can those living in the ashram regularly go outside? Author- No, absolutely not.. The Batuks cannot go outside at all. The outsiders who are there can order things through them. Question- Did you have any prior information about Ashutosh Brahmachari? Author- No, I don't know Ashutosh Maharaj. Now that there's such a commotion, I've come to know about Ashutosh Maharaj. Question- Allegations against Shankaracharya only surfaced after the Magh Mela, what do you think? Author. Well, this is possible. No possibility can be ruled out. Question - Did Shankaracharya return to Kashi from Magh Mela without bathing? Author - The highest religious authority residing on the seat of that ashram, you did not go to bathe because you were not carried by a palanquin. This is absolute nonsense. Our people who live abroad travel thousands of kilometers just to bathe. They say, even if you take a dip in someone's name, they get the merit. But Shankaracharya stayed on the bank, did not bathe. Pontoon bridges are built from the Jhunsi side so that people can reach the Sangam. Even people who cannot walk properly walk hundreds of kilometers to bathe. Question - When Shankaracharya is not present, who takes care of the ashram? Author - There is managing staff there. There is a manager Mishra, along with Didi. They oversee the entire arrangement. Question - Who is that Didi? Author - I myself asked her that this ashram is said to belong to Shankaracharya. But, you are said to be the owner. Are you his mother? Are you his sister? Are you any relative of his? Then she smiled and said, "You can consider me Shankaracharya's friend." Question - What would you say about the allegations of sexual harassment against Shankaracharya? Author - No, I cannot say anything about this. Because Shankaracharya was not there when I was there. I have no information about this.

stories.title: Dubai airspace closure halts 14 Lucknow-Gulf flights:2,500 passengers affected; international terminal remains deserted all day
stories.summary: Rising military tension in the Gulf and closure of Dubai airspace severely disrupted flight operations at Lucknow’s Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport on March 1, 2026. All scheduled arrivals and departures between Lucknow and Gulf countries were cancelled from 12 AM to 10 PM (00:00–22:00 IST), with airlines clearly citing “Dubai airspace closure” as the reason. According to airport authorities, a total of 14 major international flights—both incoming and outgoing—were cancelled, affecting nearly 2,500 passengers. As a result, the Terminal-3 building, designated for international operations, remained completely deserted throughout the day. T-3 terminal wore a deserted look The international Terminal-3 remained unusually quiet, with no aircraft arriving from Gulf nations or departing from Lucknow. Under normal circumstances, nine flights depart daily from Lucknow to Gulf destinations, while eight flights arrive from there. Passengers crowd inquiry counters, relatives anxious Following the cancellations, large numbers of passengers gathered at airline inquiry counters seeking updates. Those with scheduled travel on March 1 or in the coming days appeared especially anxious. Relatives of passengers stranded in Gulf countries also continued visiting the airport in search of information. Fresh bookings suspended until March 8 Airlines have informed passengers that new ticket bookings for Gulf routes will remain suspended until March 8, or until the situation stabilises. In the meantime, affected passengers are being offered options of full refunds or rescheduling.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri extends support to Shankaracharya amid dispute:Says, 'he backs cow protection campaign but has not been invited to Lucknow yet'
stories.summary: Bageshwar Dham's head priest, Pandit Dhirendra Shastri, has supported Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. He said, I stand with all saints who speak about Gaumata, Geeta, and Sanatan. Bageshwar Baba said, Shankaracharya has raised the cow issue. There is a campaign going on across the country regarding Mother Cow. As cow servants, we morally support him. However, we have not received an invitation for Lucknow. I am going for a one-month solitude retreat. Dhirendra Shastri arrived in Kashi with his mother on Friday. He performed worship of Baba Vishwanath. During this time, people kept taking selfies with him. Amid the conflict with CM Yogi, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand will hold an assembly in Lucknow on March 11 for the protection of the cow, Ganga, and Sanatan. However, he has not yet received permission for the assembly. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya was also in Kashi. Journalists asked him - Will Shankaracharya get permission to hold the assembly? To this, Keshav said - Giving permission is not my job. After this, he remained silent on this issue. Dhirendra Shastri gave a message to followers to live a positive life Pandit Dhirendra Shastri spoke to his followers. He gave them a message about religion, faith, and living a positive life. He said that coming to Kashi is always a special experience for him because it is the city of Lord Shiva, and its spiritual energy inspires the entire country. He congratulated the entire Indian cricket team for reaching the final. He expressed confidence that the Indian team will definitely achieve victory and make the country proud. Dhirendra Shastri also said, Path of peace will emerge from India: Peace can come to the whole world through India's Sanatan ideology. The culture of Sanatan has the power to create peace and balance in the world. Donald Trump is not trustworthy: US President Donald Trump is not trustworthy. He says one thing in the evening and something else in the morning; such a person can never be trusted. The way he misused his authority to start a tariff war shows his working style, that he wants to spread unrest in the world. The end of war and unrest in the Middle East can only happen by following the path of Sanatan. Where is Baba Bageshwar going for solitude? Dhirendra Krishna Shastri will stay away from public contact for one month. He will perform meditation in the snowy mountains of Badrinath in May. During this time, he will not be on any network, will not be present at the temple, and will not organize any katha or divine court. Dhirendra Shastri said, At the turning point where he stands, self-meditation is very necessary. New paths to distract come daily, in such times self-penance and self-meditation are essential.Dhirendra Shastri says - Will give up mobile, TV programsBaba Bageshwar clarified that he is giving up all public activities like mobile, TV, interviews, meetings and discourses. His aim is to return after one month of meditation with new energy, new thoughts and new preparation, so that he can renew himself afresh. Dhirendra Shastri will stay away from public contact for a month. He will meditate in the mountains of Badrinath.Immersed in Navratri meditation from March 17 to 27Before going for meditation, Dhirendra Shastri has some upcoming programs scheduled. He will stay at Bageshwar Dham until March 13. The schedule includes Pretraj Sarkar's court on March 7, initiation ceremony on March 8 and 9, court on Tuesday March 10, meeting with daughter-son-in-law on March 11 and 12, and havan at 9 PM on March 12. Court meeting will be held on March 13.After this, he will hold Divine Court at Sanatan Math in Mumbai from March 14 to 16. From March 17 to 27, he will be immersed in Navratri meditation, following which he will travel to Badrinath in May. Now know about Shankaracharya's program...Shankaracharya said - Yogi has 6 days leftShankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said on Thursday that CM Yogi has 6 days left. He should declare cow as the national mother. So far no statement has come from him. Other people from his party are supporting, but no one is coming forward openly.Now read about Shankaracharya's journeyShankaracharya had said that he will hold a meeting in Lucknow on March 11 for the protection of cow and Sanatan. On March 6, there will be worship of Bade Bhagwan Chinta Ganesh. On the same day, they will take a pledge on Veer Shiromani Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Jayanti. Then on the evening of March 7, they will recite Hanuman Chalisa at Sankat Mochan temple.After this, will depart for the Lucknow journey. Passing through several districts and taking night halts, will reach Lucknow on March 10. Here on March 11, on Sheetala Ashtami, Gau Dhwaj will be consecrated at Kashiram Ground. After this, the religious battle will begin - whoever wants to come for the protection of mother cow, they should come. Read Shankaracharya's travel route… Now understand the Shankaracharya controversy...There was a dispute between Shankaracharya and the administration on January 18 during Mauni Amavasya at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. 8 days later, on January 24, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj complained to the Police Commissioner. In this, allegations of sexual exploitation of children were made during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025.Alleging inaction by the police, a petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8. Two children were presented in court on February 13. Their statements were recorded on February 21. On the court's order, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station the same day. In the FIR, Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand and 2-3 unknown accused were named. On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On February 27, the High Court granted bail to Shankaracharya.

stories.title: Brother kills twin sister in Moradabad:25-year-old man also stabs mother with knife
stories.summary: A 25-year-old engineer allegedly killed his twin sister in Moradabad on Friday and later attacked his mother with a knife when she discovered the crime. The incident occurred in the Majhola police station area. According to the information, the accused Hardik Malhotra murdered his sister Himshikha (25) at their home during the afternoon. After committing the crime, Hardik reportedly drove to his mother Neelima’s office and brought her home. When Neelima entered the house, she saw her daughter lying in a pool of blood and began screaming. Hearing the noise, Hardik allegedly attacked his mother with a knife as well. Two women from the neighbourhood rushed to the house after hearing the screams. Seeing them arrive, the accused fled the scene in a car. The neighbours later found both mother and daughter severely injured and bleeding on the floor and immediately informed the police. Sister declared dead in hospital Police rushed the victims to Moradabad District Hospital, where doctors declared Himshikha dead. Their mother Neelima is currently undergoing treatment at the hospital. Police have launched a search operation to arrest the accused, who remains absconding. Brother and sister were twins The victims were twin siblings and both engineers working in Gurugram. Their mother Neelima works at an insurance company. According to SP City Ran Vijay Singh, the incident occurred following an argument between the siblings. Family background Neelima originally belongs to Badaun district. Her husband Indrajeet left the family about nine years ago, after which she moved to Buddhi Vihar in Moradabad, where she has been living alone in a rented house near Aryan International School. Job loss and Holi visit Police said Hardik had lost his job three months ago and had been living with his sister since then in Gurugram. According to neighbours, the brother and sister had come to Moradabad on March 2 to celebrate Holi with their mother and were scheduled to return to Gurugram the same day the incident occurred. Neighbour Sunita Ahluwalia said she saw Hardik bringing his mother home in a car. Soon after Neelima entered the house, loud screams were heard, prompting neighbours to rush in. Police investigation underway Police reached the spot soon after receiving the information and began an investigation. Authorities say teams have been deployed to locate and arrest the accused, while the injured mother’s statement will play a key role in the probe.

stories.title: Amitabh Bachchan buys third property in Ayodhya:₹35 crore deal for 2.67 acres; total investment in the city reaches ₹90 crore
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan has bought another large property in Ayodhya, the birthplace of the Ram Mandir. He has purchased 2.67 acres of land from 'House of Abhinandan Lodha' (HoABL). The deal is valued at ₹35 crore. The company officially announced this investment on March 6. This is Amitabh Bachchan's third major investment in Ayodhya. This land is located near the 75-acre 'The Saryu' project. Rajesh Yadav, Managing Director of Amitabh's company 'AB Corp Ltd, finalised this entire deal. This is Amitabh Bachchan's fourth real estate project overall with the Abhinandan Lodha Group. Three Plots Bought in the Last One and a Half Years Amitabh Bachchan is continuously investing in Ayodhya. Earlier, in May 2025, he had bought a 25,000 sq ft plot near 'The Saryu' for ₹40 crore. In 2024, he had acquired a 10,000 sq ft plot in the same project for ₹14.5 crore. So far, he has spent approximately ₹90 crore on land in the temple town. Viewing Land as Heritage On this investment, Abhinandan Lodha, Chairman of 'House of Abhinandan Lodha', said, "Amitabh Bachchan's investment reflects our belief in viewing land as an asset that retains value across generations. Ayodhya is a confluence of faith and heritage. Due to infrastructure development, this city has emerged as an attractive destination for investment." Already invested 10 crore rupees in Alibaug Besides Ayodhya, Big B has also invested ₹10 crore in Alibaug's 'Soul de Alibaug' project. There, he has bought 10,000 square feet of land. Bollywood actresses Kriti Sanon and Kartik Aaryan have also bought their plots in the same project in Alibaug. Prices increased 4.5 times in 5 years Land prices in Ayodhya have seen a significant jump in the last 5 years. After the International Airport, improved road connectivity, and the construction of the Ram Temple, land rates around the Saryu River bank and the Ram Temple corridor have increased by more than 4.5 times between 2020 and 2025.

stories.title: Grocery shop owner's daughter clears IAS exam:Shamli's Astha Jain secures 9th rank in UPSC after IPS selection last year
stories.summary: UPSC has released the final result of the Civil Services Exam 2025. Astha Jain from Shamli, UP has secured 9th rank in it. Astha had qualified UPSC in 2024. She became an IPS after securing 131st rank. She took leave from IPS training in Hyderabad to study for the civil services. She achieved this milestone through self-study. Astha's family lives in Kandhla. Her father runs a grocery store. Mother is a housewife. There are three sisters and one brother in the family. Astha is second among them. Elder sister is a doctor, while the third sister is also pursuing MBBS. Before becoming an IPS, Astha also took coaching in Delhi for some time. After that, she did self-study. Father said - Achieved success through hard work Astha's father, Ajay Kumar, said - My daughter has achieved this position through her hard work. My one daughter is a doctor. I did not let any shortcomings happen in my daughters' education. Gave equal opportunities to daughters. Never considered anyone less. The whole family is in a happy mood due to the daughter's success. Relatives and other family members are calling to congratulate. Mother said - Daughter's dream of becoming DM has been fulfilled Mother Mamta Jain said - Today is a day of happiness. Our child had a dream of becoming a DM. Today, she has fulfilled that dream. She has already qualified for UPSC twice before. In her first attempt, she got 131st rank. In her second attempt, she got 186th rank. Now in her third attempt, she has secured 9th rank all-India. Cousin brother Gaurav Jain said - My sister is currently training in Hyderabad. She has two months of training left. She has always been bright in her studies. Her lifestyle has been very simple.

stories.title: Two killed after Fortuner hits scooter on overbridge in Gorakhpur:Accused arrested within an hour; claims Minister Sanjay Nishad is his uncle
stories.summary: Accused, who allegedly ran over two people, including an MBBS student, with a Fortuner in Gorakhpur, was seen walking confidently in police custody. In a video, two policemen are seen escorting him, while he strolls with both hands in his jeans pockets. The accused, Golden Sahni, also has several social media reels with Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad. A photo of him with the minister has surfaced online, where he captioned it “Cabinet Minister (Uncle)” and described himself as the future Block Chief of Piprauli. The incident took place on Holi night, Wednesday, when Sahni, driving the Fortuner, hit MBBS student Akash Pandey and 50-year-old Umesh Sharma on an overbridge. Akash Pandey died on the spot, while Umesh Sharma succumbed to his injuries at AIIMS late on Thursday night. Police traced and arrested Sahni about an hour after the accident and took him to the police station. At the time of his arrest, he was wearing a black shirt and jeans. However, when he was produced in court the next day, Thursday, he appeared in a white shirt, indicating he had changed clothes while in custody. First, look at the pictures of the accused VIDEO of accused threatening the girl also surfaces Another video of the accused, Golden Sahni, has emerged. In this, a girl is cursing Golden Sahni while accusing him of harassment. In response, Golden Sahni is also threatening her while using abusive language. During this, the girl is also talking about hitting him with a sandal. The accident occurred on Holi night around 10 PM at the Mohaddipur-Kauwabagh overbridge in Gorakhpur. A Fortuner car hit three to four vehicles. Other vehicles received minor impacts, while Akash and Umesh Sharma's scooter was hit hard. Upon impact, Akash was thrown into the air and collided with the bridge railing about 15 meters away, ending up hanging face down. He died on the spot. Meanwhile, Umesh Sharma was injured and fell on the road. After the accident, people from nearby areas rushed to the scene, and a crowd gathered on the overbridge. People kept making videos, but no one helped get the student down from the railing. Police arrived about 30 minutes after being informed by passersby and retrieved Akash from the railing. After this, the police took Umesh and Akash to the district hospital. Here, doctors declared Akash dead. Meanwhile, Umesh had gone into a coma. Due to his serious condition, doctors referred him to AIIMS Gorakhpur, where he also died late Thursday night during treatment. Read about those who lost their lives in the accident MBBS student was the only son of the house Akash Pandey was a resident of Bargadwan in the Dharmasinghwa police station area of Sant Kabir Nagar. His father, Devendra Nath Pandey, owns a tent shop, while his mother, Lilavati Devi, is a housewife. Akash was the only son. He was studying MBBS third year at BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur. On Holi day, Akash went to his friend Anoop's house in the evening. After having dinner there, he was returning to the hostel around 10 PM. During this time, an accident occurred on the Mohiddipur-Kauabagh overbridge. Upon receiving the information, friend Anoop reached the hospital and started crying bitterly. He pleaded with the doctors - “Sir, please save my friend.” Umesh's brother was a doctor, and worked in a private job Umesh Sharma was the brother of ophthalmologist Dr. Kamlesh Kumar Sharma, who lives near Gita Vatika. Kamlesh said that his brother Umesh, worked in a private job. He has a family, including his wife and two children - one son and one daughter. On Holi, Umesh had gone to his sister's house in Shahpur. He was returning home on his scooter around 9:30 PM. When he reached near the Mohiddipur-Kauabag overbridge, a Fortuner hit him. He had been in a coma since the accident. MBBS students hold a candlelight march at BRD At BRD Medical College on Thursday, MBBS students, along with intern doctors and other students, held a candlelight march to pay tribute. Students said that strict legal action should be taken against Golden Sahni, who is accused of the accident. A student lost his life due to negligent driving.

stories.title: 70 people suffer eye injuries during Holi chaos:5 patients in Lucknow have cornea damage, doctors say surgery may be needed
stories.summary: The number of patients arriving at Lucknow's Trauma Center, injured and wounded due to the revelry of Holi, was quite high. Among them, about 70 patients experienced sudden eye problems while playing with colors. They lost vision in their eyes, due to which they even had to be admitted. However, the relief was that they found relief as soon as treatment began. In fact, from the morning of Holi, an atmosphere of revelry and carelessness was observed on the roads. Consequently, long queues of injured people formed in the emergency departments of Lucknow's KGMU Trauma Center, Balrampur, Civil, Lohia, Ram Sagar Mishra, Lokbandhu, and private hospitals. Many people sustained deep injuries to their faces and eyes. Doctors say that most people who arrived with eye problems suddenly lost their vision, and due to the colors, their eyes also stopped opening. There were also some people who, after riding bikes at high speed, injured their eyes when they got hurt. However, the relief was that none of them had their eyesight completely affected. Had to be admitted due to color getting into the eye Dr. Premraj Singh, CMS of KGMU Trauma Center, informed that a total of 248 patients reached for treatment in 24 hours during Holi. About 70 eye patients reached the Trauma Center. Among them, many people's eyes were on the verge of getting damaged due to color. Some patients had to be admitted due to serious condition. Dr. Prem Raj Singh said that the problem of infection and irritation has increased due to fine dust particles entering the eyes while throwing colors and gulal. During examination, wounds were found on the eyelids and around the eyes of many patients. Five such patients came forward whose corneas were directly affected due to color getting into their eyes. Severe infection was found in the eyes of these patients. An acid-like chemical-containing color was also found in the eye of one patient. Surgery may be required Ophthalmologist Dr. Sanjay Tevatia said that after Holi, many cases of corneal infection, eye injuries, and chemical-laden colors entering the eyes have been reported. Such patients are treated with medicines, but if the condition is serious, surgery may also be required. He said that dust particles are dangerous not only for the cornea but also for the sclera (white part of the eye). A particle entering the eye can cause a perforation in the sclera. This causes the fluid inside the eye to leak out, increasing the risk of vision impairment if not treated in time. Colors also affected the skin The effect of Holi colors was not limited to the eyes. Many people also faced skin-related problems. More than 90 patients reached the dermatology departments of hospitals complaining of itching, rashes, burning, and infection. Devesh Chandra Pandey, Chief Medical Superintendent of Civil Hospital, said that in the last two days, many patients with skin affected by Holi colors came to the emergency and OPD.

stories.title: 8 Gulf flights cancelled from Lucknow Airport:Over 450 passengers cancel tickets, struggle for refunds
stories.summary: The tension following the attack on Iran is now clearly affecting flight operations at Lucknow’s Amausi airport. Air services to Gulf countries have not yet returned to normal. On Thursday, a total of eight flights to and from Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Dammam were cancelled. The cancellations caused considerable inconvenience to passengers. Over 450 tickets cancelled, airlines issued refunds After the flight cancellations, more than 450 passengers cancelled their tickets. Airlines have so far issued refunds amounting to around ₹2.25 lakh. Several airlines have assured passengers that fresh bookings will begin once the situation returns to normal. Flight operations have been disrupted for the past few days due to the closure of airspace over Iran and Dubai. Earlier, around 17 flights from Lucknow to Gulf countries were affected. However, on Thursday the number came down to eight. Still, flight services have not yet fully returned to normal. These flights were cancelled Air India Express flight IX-193 from Lucknow to Dubai, IndiGo flight 6E-1415 to Abu Dhabi and IndiGo flight 6E-097 to Dammam were cancelled. IndiGo flight 6E-1424 from Sharjah to Lucknow, Air India Express flight IX-198 from Dubai, IndiGo flight 6E-1416 from Abu Dhabi, IndiGo flight 6E-098 from Dammam and Air India Express flight IX-194 from Dubai were also cancelled. Passengers wandered at airport seeking information After the cancellations, passengers and their relatives gathered at the counters at Amausi airport seeking information. Many passengers were seen moving from one airline counter to another to check the status of their flights. Several passengers are also facing difficulties in getting refunds. Dhirendra Singh had booked a ticket from Dubai to Lucknow, but after his flight was cancelled on March 3, he has been struggling to get the refund. Similarly, Mohammad Ikhlaq Ahmad had booked a ticket to Riyadh. His ticket was also cancelled due to the closure of airspace, but he has not yet received the refund. When he contacted the airline, he was told that the refund amount had already been transferred to the account of the ticket agent.

stories.title: Adulterated mustard oil worth ₹6 cr seized in UP:38 firms get notice; doctor warns of heart diseases
stories.summary: Large-scale adulteration has been found in edible oil being sold in Uttar Pradesh. Low-quality oils are being mixed with mustard oil, while chemicals are being added to create colour and foam before the product is sold in the market. The revelations came during action taken by the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA). The investigation led to several shocking findings. FIRs have been registered in Unnao and Muzaffarnagar, while notices have been issued to 38 oil companies and firms. Why was this action taken? What kind of adulteration or shortcomings were found? How many firms were inspected during the campaign? How much oil was seized and how many FIRs were filed? Read this report to know more… Teams from other districts conducted investigation Joint Food Commissioner Harishankar Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that a large-scale campaign was carried out on the instructions of Commissioner Roshan Jacob. For the drive, teams from one district were sent to inspect units in other districts. FSDA teams reached 66 units in total, of which eight were found closed. Action was taken at 58 units, from where 231 samples were collected. About 4.32 lakh litres of oil were seized, with an estimated value of ₹6.5 crore. Name of mustard, selling rice bran oil Harishankar Singh said mustard oil is expensive, and companies were selling rice bran oil (extracted from rice husk) for higher profits. The information printed on the bottle labels was also concealed. Similarly, palm oil was being sold as rice bran oil. In Unnao and Muzaffarnagar, colour and essence were being used in edible oil. Licences in both places have been suspended and FIRs registered against the company owners at local police stations. Continuous consumption of adulterated mustard oil can lead to fat accumulation in heart muscles, increasing the risk of heart attack. Deficiencies found in 38 out of 58 units inspected Harishankar Singh said that of the 58 units inspected by the FSDA, irregularities were found in 38 units. Notices have been issued to these units asking them to rectify the shortcomings. If they fail to comply, their licences will be suspended. Cases found during the inspection included mixing cheaper palm oil or rice bran oil and selling it under the label of mustard or soybean oil. Other practices included adding chemical colours, artificial flavours and argemone oil to make the oil appear pure, relabelling expired or contaminated oil with new stickers before selling it in the market, and using fake branding to sell substandard oil at higher prices. The raids were conducted at 58 units between February 20 and 28. FIRs filed in these cases 11,750 liters of mustard oil was seized from Kavya Trading Company in Budhana, Muzaffarnagar and FIR was registered. Similarly, in Bangarmau of Unnao, 3,855 liters of oil was seized and operations were shut down. FIR has also been registered after finding adulteration on a large scale. Expired mustard oil caught in Gorakhpur In Gorakhpur’s Sahjanwa area, raids were conducted at the factory and warehouse of GRL Edible Private Limited, where oil worth ₹24 lakh was seized. This included expired mustard oil worth ₹10 lakh, whose old expiry date had been replaced with a new sticker showing the year 2026. The sale of Radha Rani brand rice bran refined oil worth ₹14 lakh was also stopped. Investigators found that cheap palm oil imported from Nepal at ₹80 per litre was being mixed with chemicals and sold as mustard oil for ₹160 per litre. Health risks from consuming adulterated oil To understand the health impact of adulterated oil, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to cardiologist Dr Rohit Gupta of Gorakhpur District Hospital. He said when cheaper oils such as rice bran oil, palm oil or argemone oil and chemicals are mixed with mustard oil, it becomes extremely dangerous. Several medical studies have also shown that adulterated mustard oil can cause serious health problems. It increases the risk of heart disease, liver damage and dropsy. Harmful substances such as argemone oil present in adulterated oil can severely affect the human body.

stories.title: 8 deaths on Holi in Lucknow:248 patients reach KGMU Trauma Centre, around 800 treated in emergency within 24 hours
stories.summary: More than 800 people were injured during Holi celebrations in Lucknow. Most of the cases were linked to road accidents, especially those caused by drunk driving. Many people were taken to hospitals across the city for treatment. In the last 24 hours alone, 248 injured people reached the Trauma Centre of KGMU for treatment. Doctors admitted several patients and provided medical care. Around 72 people were injured due to high-speed accidents during the Holi celebrations. Some patients also suffered health problems because of chemical colours and suspected poisoning. According to hospital sources, two critically ill patients died during treatment. One patient is still on a ventilator in critical condition. Apart from this, six people had already died before they could reach the hospital. Government hospitals treated more than 300 injured people, while around 100 patients received treatment in private hospitals. So many patients reached the Trauma Center Dr. Premraj, Chief Medical Superintendent of the Trauma Center located at KGMU, stated that 248 people came for treatment, and among them, 75 to 80 people were injured in road accidents. Of these, about 40 people were injured in road accidents due to alcohol consumption. 365 patients reached Balrampur Dr. Himanshu Chaturvedi, CMS of Balrampur Hospital, informed that 365 patients arrived at the emergency OPD. Out of these, 51 patients needed to be admitted. The rest were sent home after providing primary treatment. 21 injured people needed stitches. He informed that 73 people came to get rabies injections during Holi. Out of these, 70 percent were old patients and 30 percent were new patients. 487 patients came to Lokbandhu Dr. Ajay Shankar Tripathi, Medical Superintendent of Lokbandhu Rajnarayan Hospital, informed that 487 patients came to the emergency in 24 hours. Out of these, 60 people were injured in road accidents during Holi. 37 patients were admitted and provided treatment. The remaining patients were sent home after primary treatment. 70 patients came to Civil Hospital. Out of these, 17 patients have been admitted and are being provided treatment. 246 patients reached Lohia 246 patients arrived at the emergency OPD of Lohia Institute. Treatment was provided to 75 patients in the surgery department. Two serious patients were admitted to the ICU. Three patients were admitted. The remaining patients were discharged after primary treatment. 27 injured patients arrived in the orthopedics department. While 144 patients arrived in the emergency medicine department. Two serious patients are admitted in critical condition. A total of 30 patients have been admitted. 74 Patients headed to SGPGI 74 injured patients arrived at SGPGI's Apex Trauma Center. Of these, more than 20 patients needed to be admitted. The remaining patients were discharged after treatment. More than 75 patients were admitted and provided treatment at Rani Laxmibai, Thakurganj Joint Hospital, Mahanagar Bhaurao Deoras, and Ram Sagar Mishra Hospital located in BKT Sadhamau. Meanwhile, more than 100 patients were admitted to private hospitals in the city. Color reaction led to hospitalization Many patients had also arrived with problems like eye irritation, etc., due to the side effects of colors, and were discharged after immediate treatment. According to the data released by Lohia Institute, around 52 patients fell victim to the revelry of Holi and reached the emergency for treatment.

stories.title: 'I am from staff let me go' says drunk SI:Crowd surrounds him in Shahjahanpur after bike collision; constables carry him away
stories.summary: In Shahjahanpur, a sub-inspector, drunk and driving a car, hit a bike. The young man riding the bike was injured. After the accident, the crowd surrounded the sub-inspector's car. When asked to get out, the sub-inspector said he was "staff." Hearing this, people got agitated and started creating a ruckus. Meanwhile, people called the police. When two constables arrived at the scene and started taking the drunk sub-inspector away from the clutches of the crowd, the sub-inspector began to stumble. During this, the crowd also tried to free the sub-inspector by pushing and shoving. Seeing the situation worsen, both constables carried the sub-inspector to the police station. People made a video of this entire incident. The accident occurred in the Banda police station area. The injured bike rider has been admitted to the hospital. His two daughters were also on the bike, who narrowly escaped. See 2 pictures of the commotion Now know the full story Sunil, a resident of Utra Tikri, was going to Khutar on his bike with his two daughters, Parul and Saloni, on Thursday. Around 1 PM, near the main intersection of Banda, his bike was hit by a Swift car (UP14 FC 3337). Sunil was injured in this accident. However, his daughters narrowly escaped. After the accident, people surrounded the car. A police cap was kept on the dashboard of the car. Upon opening the door, it was found that the driver was Sub-Inspector Jogesh Sharma, posted at Banda police station. He was going to perform his duty in his area by car. People did not let the sub-inspector close the car door When people asked the sub-inspector to come out, he folded his hands and said, "I am staff, let me go." At this, people got agitated. They started saying, "If you are staff, does that mean you can hit anyone?" Hearing this, the sub-inspector started closing the car door, but people did not let him close it. Despite much effort, the sub-inspector did not get out of the car. Meanwhile, due to the commotion of the crowd, a traffic jam started on the road. After this, someone informed the police about the incident. Following this, two constables, who were playing Holi at the police station, arrived at the scene. They somehow pulled the sub-inspector out of the car and started taking him with them. At this, people began pushing and shoving to grab the sub-inspector. However, the policemen did not let go of the sub-inspector. Sub-inspector seen stumbling In the video, the sub-inspector is seen walking unsteadily. When he couldn't walk on his own feet, both policemen carried the sub-inspector on their shoulders and took him to the police station on their bike. People alleged that Sub-inspector Jogesh was heavily intoxicated. Before hitting the bike, he had also hit the divider. Banda police station in-charge said- Sub-inspector Jogesh Sharma was going in his area. There was a minor collision, due to which three people on the bike fell. One youth sustained minor injuries. The sub-inspector also sustained minor injuries. Perhaps for this reason, he was unable to walk properly.

stories.title: 70% of Samajwadi Party’s district presidents are Muslim or Yadav:Why does Akhilesh trust more on these communities despite the PDA slogan?
stories.summary: After losing the race for power in Uttar Pradesh in 2022, the Samajwadi Party (SP) started raising the slogan of PDA, which stands for Pichda, Dalit and Muslim. The party used this slogan to strengthen its social coalition. The strategy showed results in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Out of 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh, the SP won 37 seats. Its ally Congress, which contested the election in alliance with the party, also managed to win 6 seats. After this success, many believed that the SP would reflect the PDA formula within its own organisation and bring a new political approach. It was expected that leaders from backward classes, Dalits and Muslims would get wider representation in the party structure. However, the current organisational structure tells a different story. Even today, about 70 per cent of the party’s 97 district and metropolitan presidents belong to the Yadav and Muslim communities, often referred to as the M-Y combination. This has raised questions about whether the PDA slogan has actually been implemented within the party organisation. Why is SP unable to trust beyond the M-Y equation in its organisation? What does it mean not to give a single Thakur a place in the organisation? How many upper castes has SP finally trusted? Read this report 2 posts vacant out of 97 District/Metropolitan Presidents of SP SP has a total of 97 District Presidents and Metropolitan Presidents across 18 divisions of the state. In Prayagraj, the SP has appointed three presidents for Gangapar, Yamunapar, and Prayagraj city. Among them, 2 are Muslim and one is Yadav. Additionally, District Presidents and City or Metropolitan Presidents have been appointed in Gorakhpur, Ayodhya, Lucknow, Bareilly, Moradabad, Ramnagar, Shahjahanpur, Agra, Firozabad, Mathura, Aligarh, Kanpur, Farrukhabad, Jhansi, Varanasi, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Saharanpur, and Muzaffarnagar. Out of 97 posts, the positions for Bijnor and Rampur city are currently vacant. The last major reshuffle among SP's District Presidents took place on April 7, 2023. At that time, the state leadership was in the hands of Naresh Uttam Patel. In the 2024 Lok Sabha, when SP made Naresh Uttam Patel its Lok Sabha candidate, it handed over the reins to Shyam Lal Pal, a highly backward face from the OBC community. One reason for this was also Vishwanath Pal, who was made from this community by BSP. SP feared that due to Vishwanath Pal, the Pal (Gaderia community) might distance themselves from SP. Although, it's been almost 2 years since Shyam Lal Pal became president, but so far he has been able to make only a few changes. There was a possibility of large-scale reshuffling of district presidents before the assembly elections. However, due to SIR, this is also said to be pending. 44 percent Yadavs among SP District Presidents Even though the Yadav population in the state is estimated to be between 8-9 percent, the SP has taken great care of this core vote bank in its organization. Out of the current 95 district presidents, 44 percent, meaning 42, are Yadavs. Muslims are in second place. There are Muslim district presidents in 24 places. Even though the Dalit population in the state might be 20-21 percent, only 3 Dalits have been made district presidents in the SP. During Mulayam Singh's time, Thakurs used to dominate the SP. However, currently there is not a single Thakur district president or city president. Out of 95 district presidents, only 7 positions have been given to people from the general category. Among these, there are 2 Brahmins, 2 Baniyas, and 1 each Tyagi and Bengali Kayastha. BSP state president Vishwanath Pal, while taunting SP's PDA slogan, says - the conduct, character and face of any party are visible when it is in power. SP had achieved success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections with the PDA slogan. Akhilesh Yadav himself reached the Lok Sabha by becoming an MP from an MLA. Before this, he was the leader of the opposition in the UP Assembly. He had the opportunity then to give this post to a PDA member, but he did not. The PDA slogan is being used only to get votes. Now their PDA's true colors have been exposed. Now people are looking towards BSP with hope. In 2027, under the leadership of BSP, Behan Mayawati will become the Chief Minister for the 5th time. SP relies on Muslims in the west, and Yadavs in the east SP has shown the most reliance on Muslims in Western UP. In Purvanchal, Yadavs are the most numerous district presidents. Some divisions are such where only the M-Y combination is seen. These divisions include Chitrakoot, Azamgarh, Basti, and Lucknow. However, the population of both in the state is only 27 percent. If we talk about the most balanced divisions according to the caste equation, they are the Agra and Kanpur divisions. In the Agra division, there are 7 district presidents, and posts for city and metropolitan presidents. Among these are 2 Yadav, 2 Muslim, 1 Baniya, 1 Kushwaha, and 1 Shakya district presidents. Similarly, among the 8 district presidents of Kanpur division, there are 2 each of Yadav, Muslim, and Brahmin, and 1 each of Shakya and Dalit. BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi, taking a dig, says- SP's PDA model was just a facade. Outside the family, they will not give any major responsibility to anyone. Similarly, in the organization too, they don't look beyond the M-Y equation. SP spokesperson Udayveer Singh, defending it, says- If you want to look at any organisation, you should look at it, including its state committee. District presidents are chosen based on the opinion of the people of the district. It is seen who can unite and run the organisation? As per need, reshuffles have been made in many districts from time to time. PDA does not mean that the same equation should be seen everywhere. In the state committee, it is definitely ensured that every section of society gets a place. SP cannot disturb the Yadav-Muslim ratio Senior journalist Brajesh Shukla says - SP's base has always been Yadav-Muslim. In such a situation, no party can move away from its base cadre. It is also natural to see this in SP's organisation. In elections, they certainly give fewer tickets to Yadav-Muslims compared to other castes. This was also seen in the Lok Sabha elections. Even then, SP did not make any Yadav outside the family a candidate. Similarly, they gave fewer tickets to Muslims as well. It has 4 Muslim MPs. However, more tickets were given to non-Yadav OBCs and other castes. There is no guarantee that the PDA slogan, which was popular in the Lok Sabha, will work in 2027. The aggressive stance of the Yadav community in villages is causing resentment among other castes. It may have to pay the price for this in the assembly elections. Dalits appear united with the BSP. Similarly, the BJP is also preparing to give a large number of tickets to the extremely backward classes. In such a situation, it seems difficult for PDA to remain united in favor of the SP.
